bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 春，正月，車駕上原陵。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the imperial carriage ascended to Yuanling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, the emperor traveled to Yuanling.

sentences.zh: 司徒掾陳留蔡邕曰：「吾聞古不墓祭。

translations.literal: A clerk in the office of the Minister over the Masses, Cai Yong of Chenliu, said: "I have heard that in antiquity there were no sacrifices at tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong of Chenliu, a clerk in the Secretariat of the Minister over the Masses, said, "I have heard that the ancients did not offer sacrifices at graves.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有上陵之禮，始謂可損；

translations.literal: The court has the ceremony of ascending the tombs; at first I thought it could be reduced;
translations.idiomatic: The court now observes the ceremony of visiting the imperial tombs, and I had thought it might be curtailed;

sentences.zh: 今見威儀，察其本意，乃知孝明皇帝至孝惻隱，不易奪也。

translations.literal: now seeing the majesty of the ritual and discerning its original intent, I know that Emperor Xiaoming's extreme filial piety and compassionate feeling cannot easily be taken away.
translations.idiomatic: but having witnessed the ceremony's solemn splendor and grasped its true meaning, I see that Emperor Ming's profound filial devotion and tender compassion cannot readily be set aside.

sentences.zh: 禮有煩而不可省者，此之謂也。

translations.literal: There are rites that are burdensome yet cannot be omitted—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: There are ceremonies that seem burdensome yet cannot be dispensed with—this is one of them.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬戌，太傅胡廣薨，年八十二。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day renxu, Grand Tutor Hu Guang died at the age of eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day renxu, Grand Tutor Hu Guang passed away at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 廣周流四公，三十餘年，歷事六帝，禮任極優，罷免未嘗滿歲，輒復升進。

translations.literal: Guang moved among the Four Excellencies for more than thirty years, served six emperors, received the utmost favor in ritual and appointment; whenever dismissed, before a full year had passed he was promoted again.
translations.idiomatic: For more than thirty years Hu Guang held one of the four highest offices in turn, serving six emperors with extraordinary honors; whenever he was dismissed, he was reappointed before a year had elapsed.

sentences.zh: 所辟多天下名士，與故吏陳蕃、李鹹並為三司。

translations.literal: Those he recommended were mostly famous scholars under Heaven; together with his former subordinates Chen Fan and Li Xian he served concurrently as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those he recommended were eminent men from across the realm; he and his former retainers Chen Fan and Li Xian all rose to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 練達故事，明解朝章，故京師諺曰：「萬事不理，問伯始；

translations.literal: Skilled in precedents, clear in court regulations, hence the proverb of the capital says: "When nothing is settled, ask Boshi;
translations.idiomatic: Thoroughly versed in precedent and fluent in court protocol, the capital had a saying: "When nothing gets done, ask Boshi;

sentences.zh: 天下中庸，有胡公。

translations.literal: for moderation under Heaven, there is Lord Hu."
translations.idiomatic: and for steady moderation under Heaven, there is Lord Hu."

sentences.zh: 」然溫柔謹愨，常遜言恭色以取媚於時，無忠直之風，天下以此薄之。

translations.literal: Yet gentle and cautious, he often used submissive words and deferential demeanor to curry favor with the times, without a spirit of loyal forthrightness; the world on this account held him in low esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was so mild and circumspect, always softening his speech and manner to win favor, that he lacked any spirit of loyal forthrightness, and the empire looked down on him for it.

sentences.zh: 五月，己巳，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day jisi, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven, and the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day jisi, the emperor proclaimed an amnesty throughout the realm and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 長樂太僕侯覽坐專權驕奢，策收印綬，自殺。

translations.literal: Hou Lan, Grand Steward of Changle, was charged with monopolizing power and arrogant extravagance; by edict his seal and cord were seized, and he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Lan, grand steward of Changle, was convicted of monopolizing power and arrogant excess; his seals were stripped by imperial decree, and he took his own life.

sentences.zh: 六月，京師大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the capital suffered great flooding.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, catastrophic floods struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 竇太后母卒於比景，太后憂思感疾，癸巳，崩於雲台。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager Dou's mother died at Bijing; the empress dowager, stricken with grief and illness, on the day guisi died at Yuntai.
translations.idiomatic: The mother of Empress Dowager Dou died at Bijing; overcome with grief, the empress dowager fell ill, and on the day guisi she died at Yuntai Terrace.

sentences.zh: 宦者積怨竇氏，以衣車載太后屍置城南市捨，數日，曹節、王甫欲用貴人禮殯。

translations.literal: The eunuchs, nursing long grievances against the Dou clan, carried the empress dowager's corpse on a clothes-cart and placed it in a lodge at the southern market of the city; after several days, Cao Jie and Wang Fu wished to bury her with the rites of an imperial concubine.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs, who had long nursed hatred for the Dou clan, loaded the empress dowager's body onto an ordinary cart and left it at an inn in the southern market. Days later, Cao Jie and Wang Fu proposed burying her with the rites due an imperial concubine.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「太后親立朕躬，統承大業，豈宜以貴人終乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The empress dowager personally established me on the throne and entrusted me with the great enterprise—how can she be sent off as a mere concubine!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The empress dowager personally placed me on the throne and entrusted me with the imperial succession—how can she be laid to rest with the rites of a mere concubine!

sentences.zh: 」於是發喪成禮。

translations.literal: " Thereupon mourning was proclaimed and the rites completed.
translations.idiomatic: " Mourning was then proclaimed and the funeral rites carried out.

sentences.zh: 節等欲別葬太后，而以馮貴人配祔。

translations.literal: Jie and the others wished to bury the empress dowager separately and have Lady Feng share the altar tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie and his faction wished to bury the empress dowager separately and install Lady Feng as consort in the imperial shrine instead.

sentences.zh: 詔公卿大會朝堂，令中常侍趙忠監議。

translations.literal: An edict summoned the excellencies and ministers to assemble in the court hall and ordered the Regular Palace Attendant Zhao Zhong to supervise the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the chief ministers to assemble in the court hall and appointed the palace attendant Zhao Zhong to preside over the deliberation.

sentences.zh: 太尉李鹹時病，扶輿而起，搗椒自隨，謂妻子曰：「若皇太后不得配食桓帝，吾不生還矣！

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Li Xian was then ill; he had himself carried in a litter to rise, brought pounded pepper with him, and said to his wife and children: "If the empress dowager is not granted sacrificial pairing with Emperor Huan, I shall not return alive!
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Li Xian was then gravely ill; he had himself carried in a litter to attend, brought pounded pepper to sustain himself, and told his wife and children, "If the empress dowager is not granted a place beside Emperor Huan in the ancestral shrine, I shall not return alive!

sentences.zh: 」既議，坐者數百人，各瞻望良久，莫肯先言。

translations.literal: " When the deliberation began, several hundred men were seated; each looked about for a long time, none willing to speak first.
translations.idiomatic: " When the deliberation began, several hundred officials were present; each looked about in silence for a long time, none daring to speak first.

sentences.zh: 趙忠曰：「議當時定！

translations.literal: Zhao Zhong said: "The deliberation must be settled at once!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhong said, "This matter must be settled at once!

sentences.zh: 」廷尉陳球曰：「皇太后以盛德良家，母臨天下，宜配先帝，是無所疑。

translations.literal: " Minister of Justice Chen Qiu said: "The empress dowager, of eminent virtue from a good family, ruled as mother over all under Heaven; she should be paired with the former emperor—there is no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Justice Chen Qiu said, "The empress dowager, a woman of eminent virtue from an honorable house who ruled as mother over the realm, ought to be enshrined beside the late emperor. On that there can be no doubt.

sentences.zh: 」忠笑而言曰：「陳廷尉宜便操筆。

translations.literal: " Zhong smiled and said: "Minister of Justice Chen had best take up his brush at once.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhong smiled and said, "Minister of Justice Chen, you had best take up your brush at once.

sentences.zh: 」球即下議曰：「皇太后自在椒房，有聰明母儀之德；

translations.literal: " Qiu immediately submitted a memorial saying: "Since the empress dowager was in the inner palace, she possessed the virtue of a wise and motherly exemplar;
translations.idiomatic: " Qiu immediately drafted a memorial stating, "From the time the empress dowager entered the inner palace, she displayed the wisdom and dignity of a true mother of the state;

sentences.zh: 遭時不造，援立聖明承繼宗廟，功烈至重。

translations.literal: meeting an unpropitious age, she supported the enthronement of a sage and bright heir to continue the ancestral temple—her merit and achievement were of the utmost weight.
translations.idiomatic: in an age of turmoil she raised a worthy sovereign to continue the imperial line, a service of the greatest weight.

sentences.zh: 先帝晏駕，因遇大獄，遷居空宮，不幸早世，家雖獲罪，事非太后，今若別葬，誠失天下之望。

translations.literal: When the former emperor passed away, she encountered a great persecution, was moved to an empty palace, and unfortunately died young; though her family was punished, the matter did not involve the empress dowager herself—if she is now buried separately, it will truly disappoint the hopes of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: After the late emperor's death she suffered a great persecution and was confined to an empty palace; she died before her time. Though her family was punished, she herself was guilty of nothing. To bury her separately now would truly disappoint the hopes of the empire.

sentences.zh: 且馮貴人塚嘗被發掘，骸骨暴露，與賊並屍，魂靈污染，且無功於國，何宜上配至尊！

translations.literal: Moreover, Lady Feng's tomb was once excavated, her bones exposed, her corpse mingled with bandits—her spirit defiled—and she had no merit to the state; how can she be installed to share sacrifice with the Supreme One!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Lady Feng's tomb was once robbed open, her bones left exposed and mingled with thieves—a spirit defiled—and she rendered no service to the state. How can she be installed to share the imperial shrine with the Son of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 」忠省球議，作色俯仰，蚩球曰：「陳廷尉建此議甚健！

translations.literal: " Zhong read Qiu's proposal, changed expression looking up and down, and ridiculed Qiu, saying: "Minister of Justice Chen has framed this proposal very boldly!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhong reviewed Qiu's memorial, his face shifting as he glanced about, and mocked him: "Minister of Justice Chen, what a vigorous memorial you have drafted!

sentences.zh: 」球曰：「陳、竇既冤，皇太后無故幽閉，臣常痛心，天下憤歎！

translations.literal: " Qiu said: "Chen and Dou were already wronged; the empress dowager was confined without cause—I have long been pained at heart, and all under Heaven have sighed in anger!
translations.idiomatic: " Qiu said, "Chen Fan and Dou Wu were wronged, and the empress dowager was confined without cause. I have long grieved over this, and the empire has groaned in indignation!

sentences.zh: 今日言之，退而受罪，宿昔之願也！

translations.literal: To speak of it today and afterward accept punishment is a wish I have long cherished!
translations.idiomatic: To speak out today and accept whatever punishment follows is a wish I have cherished for years!

sentences.zh: 」李鹹曰：「臣本謂宜爾，誠與意合。

translations.literal: " Li Xian said: "Your servant originally held that it should be so; this truly accords with my intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xian said, "I have long held that this was the right course, and your proposal accords perfectly with my own view.

sentences.zh: 」於是公卿以下皆從球議。

translations.literal: " Thereupon all from the excellencies down followed Qiu's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon all the ministers from the excellencies down sided with Qiu.

sentences.zh: 曹節、王甫猶爭，以為：「梁後家犯惡逆，別葬懿陵，武帝黜廢衛後，而以李夫人配食，今竇氏罪深，豈得合葬先帝！

translations.literal: Cao Jie and Wang Fu still contended, holding: "The family of Empress Liang committed wicked treason and was buried separately at Yiling; Emperor Wu deposed and cast aside Empress Wei and had Lady Li share the sacrifices—now the Dou clan's crime is deep; how can they be buried together with the former emperor!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie and Wang Fu still objected, arguing, "When the Liang empress's family committed treason, she was buried separately at Yiling. Emperor Wu deposed Empress Wei and installed Lady Li in the shrine instead. The Dou clan's crimes run far deeper—how can they be buried with the late emperor!

sentences.zh: 」李鹹復上疏曰：「臣伏惟章德竇後虐害恭懷，安思閻後家犯惡逆，而和帝無異葬之議，順朝無貶降之文。

translations.literal: " Li Xian submitted another memorial saying: "Your servant respectfully considers that Empress Zhangde Dou maltreated Gonghuai, and the family of Empress Ansi Yan committed wicked treason, yet Emperor He had no proposal for separate burial, and the court of Emperor Shun issued no text of degradation.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xian submitted another memorial: "I reflect that Empress Zhangde Dou maltreated the heir Gonghuai, and the family of Empress Ansi Yan committed treason, yet Emperor He never proposed a separate burial, and Emperor Shun's court issued no decree degrading them.

sentences.zh: 至於衛後，孝武皇帝身所廢棄，不可以為比。

translations.literal: As for Empress Wei, Emperor Xiaowu personally cast her aside—she cannot serve as a comparison.
translations.idiomatic: As for Empress Wei, she was personally cast aside by Emperor Wu and is not a valid precedent.

sentences.zh: 今長樂太后尊號在身，親嘗稱制，且援立聖明，光隆皇祚。

translations.literal: Now the Changle empress dowager bears her exalted title, personally once held regency, and moreover supported the enthronement of a sage and bright ruler, gloriously elevating the imperial succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Changle empress dowager still bears her exalted title, once held regency in person, and raised a worthy sovereign to the throne, gloriously securing the imperial succession.

sentences.zh: 太后以陛下為子，陛下豈得不以太后為母！

translations.literal: The empress dowager took Your Majesty as her son—how can Your Majesty fail to take the empress dowager as your mother!
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager took Your Majesty as her son—how can Your Majesty refuse to honor her as your mother!

sentences.zh: 子無黜母，臣無貶君，宜合葬宣陵，一如舊制。

translations.literal: A son does not dismiss his mother; a subject does not degrade his ruler—she should be buried together at Xuanling, just as in the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: A son does not disown his mother, nor may a subject degrade his sovereign. She should be buried at Xuanling according to the established rites.

sentences.zh: 」帝省奏，從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor reviewed the memorial and assented.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor read the memorial and agreed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲寅，葬桓思皇后於宣陵。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jiayin, Empress Huansi was buried at Xuanling.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day jiayin, Empress Huansi was buried at Xuanling.

sentences.zh: 有人書朱雀闕，言：「天下大亂，曹節、王甫幽殺太后，公卿皆尸祿，無忠言者。

translations.literal: Someone wrote on the Vermilion Bird Gate, saying: "All under Heaven is in great disorder; Cao Jie and Wang Fu secretly killed the empress dowager; the excellencies and ministers all hold salaries like corpses, with none offering loyal words.
translations.idiomatic: Someone wrote on the Vermilion Bird Gate: "The realm is in chaos. Cao Jie and Wang Fu murdered the empress dowager in secret. The chief ministers all draw salaries like dead men, and none speaks with loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」詔司隸校尉劉猛逐捕，十日一會。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Director of Retainers Liu Meng to pursue and arrest the culprit, with reports due every ten days.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered Director of Retainers Liu Meng to hunt down the author, with progress reports due every ten days.

sentences.zh: 猛以誹書言直，不肯急捕。

translations.literal: Meng, considering the seditious writing to speak frankly, refused to pursue the arrest urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, judging the inscription to speak plain truth, refused to press the search.

sentences.zh: 月餘，主名不立；

translations.literal: After more than a month, the principal's name was not established;
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month, the culprit had not been found;

sentences.zh: 猛坐左轉諫議大夫，以御史中丞段熲代之。

translations.literal: Meng was demoted to the left and made Grand Master of Remonstrance; Imperial Secretary Duan Yong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng was demoted to Grand Master of Remonstrance on the left, and Imperial Secretary Duan Yong was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 熲乃四出逐捕，及太學游生系者千餘人。

translations.literal: Yong then sent pursuers in all four directions; more than a thousand wandering students of the Imperial Academy were detained.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent agents in all directions to hunt down suspects, and more than a thousand students of the Imperial Academy were arrested.

sentences.zh: 節等又使熲以它事奏猛，論輸左校。

translations.literal: Jie and the others also had Yong memorialize against Meng on another matter; he was sentenced and sent to the Left Barracks.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie and his faction also had Yong impeach Meng on another charge, and Meng was sentenced to hard labor in the Left Barracks.

sentences.zh: 初，司隸校尉王寓依倚宦官，求薦於太常張奐，奐拒之，寓遂陷奐以黨罪禁錮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Director of Retainers Wang Yu relied on the eunuchs and sought recommendation from Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhang Huan; Huan refused him, and Yu then framed Huan with the crime of faction and had him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Director of Retainers Wang Yu had relied on the eunuchs and sought a recommendation from Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhang Huan. Huan refused, and Yu then framed him for factionalism and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 奐嘗與段熲爭擊羌，不相平，熲為司隸，欲逐奐歸敦煌而害之；

translations.literal: Huan had once disputed with Duan Yong over campaigns against the Qiang and bore him no goodwill; when Yong became Director of Retainers, he wished to drive Huan back to Dunhuang and harm him;
translations.idiomatic: Huan had once clashed with Duan Yong over the Qiang campaigns and bore him a grudge. When Yong became Director of Retainers, he sought to drive Huan back to Dunhuang and destroy him;

sentences.zh: 奐奏記哀請於熲，乃得免。

translations.literal: Huan submitted a letter pleading piteously to Yong and thereby escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Huan submitted a humble plea to Yong and was spared.

sentences.zh: 初，魏郡李暠為司隸校尉，以舊怨殺扶風蘇謙；

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Hao of Wei Commandery, as Director of Retainers, killed Su Qian of Fufeng over an old grievance;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Hao of Wei Commandery, while serving as Director of Retainers, killed Su Qian of Fufeng over an old grudge;

sentences.zh: 謙子不韋瘞而不葬，變姓名，結客報仇。

translations.literal: Qian's son Buwei buried the body but held no funeral, changed his name, gathered clients, and sought revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's son Buwei buried the body but withheld the funeral rites, assumed a false name, gathered followers, and plotted revenge.

sentences.zh: 暠遷大司農，不韋匿於諭廥中，鑿地旁達暠之寢室，殺其妾並小兒。

translations.literal: When Hao was transferred to Grand Minister of Agriculture, Buwei hid in the granary office, tunneled underground to reach Hao's bedchamber, and killed his concubine and young children.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was promoted to Grand Minister of Agriculture, Buwei hid in the granary offices, tunneled into Hao's bedchamber, and killed his concubine and children.

sentences.zh: 暠大懼，以板藉地，一夕九徙。

translations.literal: Hao was greatly afraid; he laid boards on the ground and moved his bed nine times in one night.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was terrified; he slept on boards laid over the floor and moved his bed nine times in a single night.

sentences.zh: 又掘暠父塚，斷取其頭，標之於市。

translations.literal: He also excavated Hao's father's tomb, severed and took the head, and displayed it in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened Hao's father's tomb, severed the head, and displayed it in the market.

sentences.zh: 暠求捕不獲，憤恚，嘔血死。

translations.literal: Hao sought to capture him but failed; in rage and resentment he vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hao failed to capture him, and in fury and despair vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: 不韋遇赦還家，乃葬父行喪。

translations.literal: Buwei encountered an amnesty and returned home, then buried his father and observed mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Buwei was pardoned and returned home, where he at last buried his father and observed the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 張奐素睦於蘇氏，而段熲與暠善，熲辟不韋為司隸從事，不韋懼，稱病不詣。

translations.literal: Zhang Huan had long been on friendly terms with the Su clan, while Duan Yong had been close to Hao; Yong appointed Buwei as an aide in the office of the Director of Retainers, and Buwei, afraid, pleaded illness and did not report.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huan had long been friendly with the Su clan, while Duan Yong had been close to Li Hao. Yong appointed Buwei as an aide in the Director of Retainers' office; Buwei, fearing for his life, pleaded illness and did not report.

sentences.zh: 熲怒，使從事張賢就家殺之，先以鴆與賢父曰：「若賢不得不韋，便可飲此！

translations.literal: Yong was enraged and sent his aide Zhang Xian to kill Buwei at his home; he first gave poison to Xian's father, saying: "If Xian cannot get Buwei, you may drink this!
translations.idiomatic: Yong was furious and sent his aide Zhang Xian to kill Buwei at his home. He first gave poison to Xian's father, saying, "If Xian fails to capture Buwei, you may drink this!

sentences.zh: 」賢遂收不韋，並其一門六十餘人，盡誅之。

translations.literal: " Xian then seized Buwei and, together with more than sixty members of his entire clan, put them all to death.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian then arrested Buwei and executed him together with more than sixty members of his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 渤海王悝之貶癭陶也，因中常侍王甫求復國，許謝錢五千萬；

translations.literal: When Prince Kui of Bohai was demoted to Yingtao, through the Regular Palace Attendant Wang Fu he sought restoration of his state and promised fifty million in gratitude money;
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kui of Bohai was demoted to Yingtao, he enlisted the Regular Palace Attendant Wang Fu to seek restoration of his fief and promised fifty million cash in gratitude;

sentences.zh: 既而桓帝遺詔復悝國，悝知非甫功，不肯還謝錢。

translations.literal: Subsequently Emperor Huan's testamentary edict restored Kui's state; Kui knew it was not Fu's doing and refused to repay the gratitude money.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huan's deathbed edict later restored Kui's fief, Kui knew Wang Fu deserved no credit and refused to pay.

sentences.zh: 中常侍鄭颯、中黃門董騰數與悝交通，甫密司察以告段熲。

translations.literal: The Regular Palace Attendant Zheng Sa and the Palace Yellow Gate Attendant Dong Teng had frequent dealings with Kui; Fu secretly investigated and reported this to Duan Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The palace attendants Zheng Sa and Dong Teng had frequent contact with Kui. Wang Fu secretly investigated and reported this to Duan Yong.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，收颯送北寺獄，使尚書令廉忠誣奏「颯等謀迎立悝，大逆不道」，遂詔冀州刺史收悝考實，迫責悝，令自殺；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Sa was arrested and sent to the North Temple Prison; the Chief Minister of Writing Lian Zhong was made to memorialize falsely that "Sa and others plotted to welcome and establish Kui—great treason, against the Way"; an edict then ordered the Inspector of Jizhou to seize Kui, examine the facts, press charges against him, and compel him to kill himself;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, Sa was arrested and sent to the North Temple Prison. Chief Minister Lian Zhong was made to accuse him of plotting to install Prince Kui as emperor—a capital crime. An edict ordered the inspector of Jizhou to seize Kui, investigate, and force him to take his own life;

sentences.zh: 妃妾十一人、子女七十人、伎女二十四人皆死獄中，傅、相以下悉伏誅。

translations.literal: eleven consorts, seventy sons and daughters, and twenty-four female performers all died in prison; the tutor, chancellor, and all below were executed.
translations.idiomatic: eleven consorts, seventy children, and twenty-four female performers all died in prison; the prince's tutor, chancellor, and all his officials were executed.

sentences.zh: 甫等十二人皆以功封列侯。

translations.literal: Fu and twelve others were all enfeoffed as full marquises for their merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu and twelve others were all enfeoffed as marquises for their supposed service.

sentences.zh: 十一月，會稽妖賊許生起句章，自稱陽明皇帝，眾以萬數；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the sorcerer-rebel Xu Sheng rose at Gouzhang in Kuaiji, styled himself Emperor Yangming, and his followers numbered in the tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, the sorcerer-rebel Xu Sheng rose at Gouzhang in Kuaiji, proclaimed himself Emperor Yangming, and gathered tens of thousands of followers;

sentences.zh: 遣揚州刺史臧旻、丹楊太守陳寅討之。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yangzhou Zang Min and the Grand Administrator of Danyang Chen Yin were sent to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector of Yangzhou Zang Min and the grand administrator of Danyang Chen Yin were dispatched to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，司徒許栩罷，以大鴻臚袁隗為司徒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Minister over the Masses Xu Xu was dismissed; Grand Herald Yuan Wei was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Minister over the Masses Xu Xu was dismissed, and Grand Herald Yuan Wei was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑寇并州。

translations.literal: The Xianbei raided Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei raided Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 是歲，單于車兒死，子屠特若屍逐就單于立。

translations.literal: This year the Chanyu Cher died; his son Tute Ruoshizhujiu was established as Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: That year the chanyu Cher died, and his son Tute Ruoshizhujiu succeeded him as chanyu.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，大疫。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, a great epidemic.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, a great epidemic swept the land.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，司空宗俱薨。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, Minister of Works Zong Ju died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou, Minister of Works Zong Ju passed away.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬午，赦天下。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day renwu, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day renwu, the emperor proclaimed an amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 以光祿勳楊賜為司空。

translations.literal: Household Minister Yang Ci was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Household Minister Yang Ci was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三月，太尉李鹹免。

translations.literal: In the third month, Grand Commandant Li Xian was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Grand Commandant Li Xian was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，以司隸校尉段熲為太尉。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, Director of Retainers Duan Yong was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, Director of Retainers Duan Yong was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 六月，北海地震。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Beihai suffered an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, an earthquake struck Beihai.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，司空楊賜免；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Minister of Works Yang Ci was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Minister of Works Yang Ci was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 以太常穎川唐珍為司空。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Tang Zhen of Yingchuan was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Ceremonies Tang Zhen of Yingchuan was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 珍，衡之弟也。

translations.literal: Zhen was the younger brother of Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was the younger brother of Heng.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，太尉段熲罷。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, Grand Commandant Duan Yong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter, Grand Commandant Duan Yong was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑寇幽、并二州。

translations.literal: The Xianbei raided the two provinces of You and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei raided You and Bing provinces.

sentences.zh: 癸酉晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On the last day of the month, the day guiyou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the month, guiyou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，己巳，赦天下。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on the day jisi, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring, on the day jisi, the emperor proclaimed an amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 以太常東海陳耽為太尉。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Chen Dan of Donghai was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Ceremonies Chen Dan of Donghai was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 三月，中山穆王暢薨，無子，國除。

translations.literal: In the third month, Prince Chang of Zhongshan died without a son, and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Prince Mu Chang of Zhongshan died without an heir, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，封河間王利子康為濟南王，奉孝仁皇祀。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, Kang, son of Prince Li of Hejian, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan to maintain the sacrifices to Emperor Xiaoren.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer, Kang, son of Prince Li of Hejian, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan to maintain the ancestral rites of Emperor Xiaoren.

sentences.zh: 吳郡司馬富春孫堅召募精勇，得千餘人，助州郡討許生。

translations.literal: Sun Jian of Fuchun, a marshal of Wu Commandery, recruited elite fighters and obtained more than a thousand men to assist the province and commanderies in attacking Xu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian of Fuchun, a marshal of Wu Commandery, recruited elite fighters and raised more than a thousand men to assist the provincial forces against Xu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，臧旻、陳寅大破生於會稽，斬之。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, Zang Min and Chen Yin inflicted a great defeat on Sheng at Kuaiji and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, Zang Min and Chen Yin routed Xu Sheng at Kuaiji and executed him.

sentences.zh: 任城王博薨，無子，國絕。

translations.literal: Prince Bo of Rencheng died without a son, and the line of the state was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bo of Rencheng died without an heir, and the fief was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 十二月，鮮卑入北地，太守夏育率屠各追擊，破之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Xianbei entered Beidi; the Grand Administrator Xia Yu led the Tuge in pursuit, defeated them, and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, the Xianbei invaded Beidi; Grand Administrator Xia Yu led the Tuge cavalry in pursuit and routed them.

sentences.zh: 遷育為護烏桓校尉。

translations.literal: Yu was transferred to be Colonel Protector of the Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yu was promoted to Colonel Protector of the Wuhuan.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑又寇并州。

translations.literal: The Xianbei again raided Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei raided Bing Province again.

sentences.zh: 司空唐珍罷，以永樂少府許訓為司空。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Tang Zhen was dismissed; Junior Steward of Yongle Xu Xun was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Tang Zhen was dismissed, and Junior Steward of Yongle Xu Xun was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，詔諸儒正《五經》文字，命議郎蔡邕為古文、篆、隸三體書之，刻石，立於太學門外，使後儒晚學鹹取正焉。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, an edict ordered the scholars to rectify the characters of the Five Classics; Palace Gentleman Cai Yong was ordered to write them in the three scripts of ancient, seal, and clerical, carve them in stone, and set them up outside the gate of the Imperial Academy, so that later scholars and late learners might all take correction from them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring, an edict ordered scholars to standardize the text of the Five Classics. Palace Gentleman Cai Yong was commissioned to write them in ancient, seal, and clerical scripts, carve them in stone, and set them up outside the Imperial Academy gate, so that future scholars might have an authoritative standard.

sentences.zh: 碑始立，其觀視及摹寫者車乘日千餘兩，填塞街陌。

translations.literal: When the steles were first erected, those who came to view and copy them numbered more than a thousand carriages a day, filling and blocking the streets.
translations.idiomatic: When the steles were first erected, more than a thousand carriages a day came to view and copy them, choking the streets.

sentences.zh: 初，朝議以州郡相黨，人情比周，乃制昏姻之家及兩州人士不得對相監臨，至是復有三互法，禁忌轉密，選用艱難，幽、冀二州久缺不補。

translations.literal: Earlier, the court debated that provinces and commanderies formed factions and men curried favor with one another; regulations were made that families joined by marriage and men from two provinces could not supervise each other reciprocally. At this time the Three Mutuals law was revived, taboos grew ever stricter, selection and appointment became difficult, and You and Ji provinces long went unfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the court had concluded that provincial officials formed factions and cultivated cliques, and decreed that men linked by marriage or from neighboring provinces could not supervise one another. Now the Three Mutuals law was revived, restrictions grew tighter, appointments became nearly impossible, and You and Ji provinces went unfilled for years.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕上疏曰：「伏見幽、冀舊壤，鎧、馬所出，比年兵饑，漸至空耗。

translations.literal: Cai Yong submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has observed that the old territories of You and Ji are sources of armor and horses; in recent years war and famine have gradually reduced them to emptiness and exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong submitted a memorial: "I observe that the old territories of You and Ji, sources of armor and horses, have been drained by years of war and famine.

sentences.zh: 今者闕職經時，吏民延屬，而三府選舉，逾月不定。

translations.literal: Now offices have stood vacant for a long time; officials and people look on in expectation, yet the Three Excellencies' selections drag on for months without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Offices there have stood vacant for a long time while officials and people wait in expectation, yet selections by the Three Excellencies drag on for months without resolution.

sentences.zh: 臣怪問其故，雲避三互。

translations.literal: Your servant asked in wonder the reason and was told it was to avoid the Three Mutuals.
translations.idiomatic: When I inquired into the cause, I was told it was to avoid violating the Three Mutuals rule.

sentences.zh: 十一月有禁，當取二州而已。

translations.literal: The prohibition of the eleventh month should apply only to taking men from the two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The prohibition should apply only to appointing men from those two provinces themselves.

sentences.zh: 又，二州之士或復限以歲月，狐疑遲淹，兩州懸空，萬里蕭條，無所管系。

translations.literal: Moreover, men of the two provinces are sometimes further restricted by time limits; in hesitation and delay the two provinces hang empty, desolate for ten thousand li, with nothing to govern or bind them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, candidates from other provinces are sometimes further delayed by time restrictions. In hesitation and delay, two vast provinces hang without governance, desolate across a thousand miles, bound to nothing.

sentences.zh: 愚以為三互之禁，禁之薄者。

translations.literal: Your servant considers the prohibition of the Three Mutuals a thin and feeble prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: I consider the Three Mutuals prohibition a feeble restraint.

sentences.zh: 今但申以威靈，明其憲令，對相部主，尚畏懼不敢營私；

translations.literal: If now authority and majesty alone are asserted and statutes made clear, counterparts supervising each other's departments still fear and dare not pursue private gain;
translations.idiomatic: If authority and law are clearly asserted, officials supervising neighboring jurisdictions still fear to pursue private gain;

sentences.zh: 況乃三互，何足為嫌！

translations.literal: how much less can the Three Mutuals be worth worrying over!
translations.idiomatic: how much less should the Three Mutuals be an obstacle!

sentences.zh: 昔韓安國起自徒中，朱買臣出於幽賤，並以才宜，還守本邦，豈復顧循三互，系以末制乎！

translations.literal: In the past Han Anguo rose from among convicts, Zhu Maichen came from obscurity and low station; both by talent and fitness returned to guard their native states—would they have again heeded the Three Mutuals and been bound by petty regulations!
translations.idiomatic: In the past Han Anguo rose from convict labor and Zhu Maichen from obscurity; both by merit returned to govern their home regions. Would they have been bound by such petty regulations as the Three Mutuals!

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下上則先帝，蠲除近禁，其諸州刺史器用可換者，無拘日月、三互，以差厥中。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty, taking the former emperors as model above, to abolish recent prohibitions; for provincial inspectors and others whose talents fit, do not bind them by time limits or the Three Mutuals, but appoint according to what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty, following the example of former emperors, to abolish these recent restrictions. For provincial inspectors whose talents fit the need, do not bind them by time limits or the Three Mutuals, but appoint as circumstances require.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷不從。

translations.literal: " The court did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: " The court did not assent.

sentences.zh: ══臣光曰：叔向有言：「國將亡，必多制。

translations.literal: ══ Master Guang remarked: Shuxiang once said: "When a state is about to perish, it must multiply regulations.
translations.idiomatic: ══ Master Guang remarked: Shuxiang once said, "When a state is about to perish, it multiplies regulations.

sentences.zh: 」明王之政，謹擇忠賢而任之，凡中外之臣，有功則賞，有罪則誅，無所阿私，法制不煩而天下大治。

translations.literal: " The government of an enlightened king carefully selects the loyal and worthy and employs them; for all ministers within and without, if they have merit they are rewarded, if guilt they are punished, with no favoritism—laws are not burdensome yet all under Heaven is greatly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: " An enlightened ruler carefully selects loyal and worthy men and employs them. Whether within or without the court, merit is rewarded and guilt punished without favoritism. Laws are few yet the realm is well governed.

sentences.zh: 所以然者何哉？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 執其本故也。

translations.literal: Because it holds to the root.
translations.idiomatic: Because it holds to fundamentals.

sentences.zh: 及其衰也，百官之任不能擇人，而禁令益多，防閒益密，有功者以閡文不賞，為奸者以巧法免誅，上下勞擾而天下大亂。

translations.literal: When it declines, the offices of the hundred officials cannot select men, yet prohibitions grow ever more numerous and barriers ever tighter; those with merit are not rewarded because of obstructive texts, wrongdoers escape punishment through crafty laws—the high and low are wearied and disturbed and all under Heaven falls into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When a state declines, offices cannot be filled with worthy men, yet prohibitions multiply and barriers tighten. The meritorious go unrewarded because of procedural obstacles; wrongdoers escape through legal loopholes. The court is exhausted and the realm falls into chaos.

sentences.zh: 所以然者何哉？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 逐其末故也。

translations.literal: Because it pursues the branch tips.
translations.idiomatic: Because it pursues secondary matters.

sentences.zh: 孝靈之時，刺史、二千石貪如豺虎，暴殄烝民，而朝廷方守三互之禁。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ling, inspectors and the two-thousand-bushel officials were greedy as wolves and tigers, wantonly destroying the people, while the court still enforced the prohibition of the Three Mutuals.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling, provincial inspectors and grand administrators were greedy as wolves and tigers, wantonly destroying the people, while the court still enforced the Three Mutuals prohibition.

sentences.zh: 以令視之，豈不適足為笑而深可為戒哉！

translations.literal: Viewed by this regulation, is it not just fit to be laughed at and deeply to be taken as a warning!
translations.idiomatic: Viewed in this light, is it not laughable—and deeply worth taking as a warning!

sentences.zh: 封河間王建孫佗為任城王。

translations.literal: Tuo, grandson of Prince Jian of Hejian, was enfeoffed as Prince of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo, grandson of Prince Jian of Hejian, was enfeoffed as Prince of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，郡、國七大水。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, seven commanderies and kingdoms suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, seven commanderies and kingdoms suffered catastrophic floods.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁卯，赦天下。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day dingmao, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day dingmao, the emperor proclaimed an amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 延陵園災。

translations.literal: The Yanling park suffered fire.
translations.idiomatic: Fire struck the Yanling park.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑寇幽州。

translations.literal: The Xianbei raided You Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei raided You Province.

sentences.zh: 六月，弘農、三輔螟。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Hongnong and the Three Metropolises suffered locusts.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, locusts struck Hongnong and the Three Metropolises.

sentences.zh: 於窴王安國攻拘彌，大破之，殺其王。

translations.literal: Anguo, king of Khotan, attacked Jumi, inflicted a great defeat, and killed its king.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo, king of Khotan, attacked Jumi, routed its forces, and killed its king.

sentences.zh: 戊己校尉、西域長史各發兵輔立拘彌侍子定興為王，人眾裁千口。

translations.literal: The Colonel Protector of the Wuji Garrison and the Chief Clerk of the Western Regions each sent troops to assist in establishing Dingxing, the attendant son of Jumi, as king; the population amounted to only a thousand mouths.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonel Protector of the Wuji Garrison and the Chief Clerk of the Western Regions each sent troops to install Dingxing, Jumi's hostage prince, as king; the population numbered barely a thousand.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸亥，赦天下。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day guihai, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the day guihai, the emperor proclaimed an amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 益州郡夷反，太守李顒討平之。

translations.literal: The tribal peoples of Yizhou commandery rebelled; the Grand Administrator Li Yong suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal peoples of Yizhou rebelled; Grand Administrator Li Yong suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 大雩。

translations.literal: A great rain prayer was held.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor performed a great rain prayer.

sentences.zh: 五月，太尉陳耽罷，以司空許訓為太尉。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Grand Commandant Chen Dan was dismissed; Minister of Works Xu Xun was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Grand Commandant Chen Dan was dismissed, and Minister of Works Xu Xun was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 閏月，永昌太守曹鸞上書曰：「夫黨人者，或耆年淵德，或衣冠英賢，皆宜股肱王室，左右大猷者也；

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, the Grand Administrator of Yongchang Cao Luan submitted a memorial saying: "The faction victims are some men of advanced years and profound virtue, some eminent worthies of official rank—all ought to be the arms and legs of the royal house, assistants in great policies;
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Grand Administrator Cao Luan of Yongchang submitted a memorial: "The men of the faction persecutions include elders of profound virtue and eminent scholars of official rank—all ought to serve as pillars of the royal house and advisers in great affairs;

sentences.zh: 而久被禁錮，辱在塗泥。

translations.literal: yet long imprisoned, disgraced in the mire.
translations.idiomatic: yet they have long been imprisoned, disgraced in the mire.

sentences.zh: 謀反大逆尚蒙赦宥，黨人何罪，獨不開恕乎！

translations.literal: Those guilty of plotting rebellion and great treason still receive pardon—what crime have the faction victims committed, that they alone are not granted forgiveness!
translations.idiomatic: Even those guilty of treason receive pardon—what crime have the faction victims committed, that they alone are denied forgiveness!

sentences.zh: 所以災異屢見，水旱荐臻，皆由於斯。

translations.literal: Hence omens and anomalies appear repeatedly, floods and droughts come in succession—all because of this.
translations.idiomatic: This is why omens multiply and floods and droughts come in succession.

sentences.zh: 宜加沛然，以副天心。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should extend abundant grace to accord with Heaven's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should extend abundant grace to accord with Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 」帝省奏，大怒，即詔司隸、益州檻車收鸞，送槐裡獄，掠殺之。

translations.literal: " The emperor read the memorial, was greatly enraged, and immediately ordered the Director of Retainers and Yizhou to seize Luan in a caged cart, send him to Huaili Prison, and torture him to death.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor read the memorial, flew into a rage, and immediately ordered the Director of Retainers and the inspector of Yizhou to seize Luan in a prison cart, send him to Huaili Prison, and torture him to death.

sentences.zh: 於是詔州郡更考黨人門生、故吏、父子、兄弟在位者，悉免官禁錮，爰及五屬。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the provinces and commanderies to re-examine faction victims' students, former subordinates, fathers, sons, and brothers in office—all were dismissed and imprisoned, extending to the five degrees of kinship.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered the provinces to re-examine the students, former subordinates, fathers, sons, and brothers in office of faction victims—all were dismissed and imprisoned, extending to five degrees of kinship.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬戌，以太常南陽劉逸為司空。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day renxu, Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Yi of Nanyang was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day renxu, Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Yi of Nanyang was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，太尉許訓罷。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Grand Commandant Xu Xun was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Grand Commandant Xu Xun was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 以光祿勳劉寬為太尉。

translations.literal: Household Minister Liu Kuan was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Household Minister Liu Kuan was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，司徒袁隗罷；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Minister over the Masses Yuan Wei was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, Minister over the Masses Yuan Wei was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙戌，以光祿大夫楊賜為司徒。

translations.literal: in the eleventh month, on the day bingxu, Household Grandee Yang Ci was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: in the eleventh month, on the day bingxu, Household Grandee Yang Ci was appointed Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 是歲，鮮卑寇幽州。

translations.literal: This year the Xianbei raided You Province.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Xianbei raided You Province.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑，赦天下。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinchou, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on the day xinchou, the emperor proclaimed an amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，大旱，七州蝗。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, great drought; locusts in seven provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, a great drought struck, and locusts ravaged seven provinces.

sentences.zh: 令三公條奏長吏苛酷貪污者，罷免之。

translations.literal: The Three Excellencies were ordered to memorialize item by item senior officials who were harsh, cruel, and corrupt, and dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies were ordered to report senior officials who were harsh, cruel, or corrupt, and have them dismissed.

sentences.zh: 平原相漁陽陽球坐嚴酷，征詣廷尉。

translations.literal: Yang Qiu of Yuyang, Chancellor of Pingyuan, was charged with harsh severity and summoned to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiu of Yuyang, chancellor of Pingyuan, was charged with harsh severity and summoned to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 帝以球前為九江太守討賊有功，特赦之，拜議郎。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Qiu had formerly as Grand Administrator of Jiujiang attacked bandits with merit, specially pardoned him and appointed him Palace Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, recalling that Yang Qiu had merit suppressing bandits as grand administrator of Jiujiang, specially pardoned him and appointed him Palace Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑寇三邊。

translations.literal: The Xianbei raided the three frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei raided the three frontier regions.

sentences.zh: 市賈小民有相聚為宣陵孝子者數十人，詔皆除太子舍人。

translations.literal: Several dozen petty market traders gathered and styled themselves filial sons of Xuanling; an edict appointed them all Attendants of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen petty market traders gathered and styled themselves filial sons mourning at Xuanling; an edict appointed them all Attendants of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，司空劉逸免，以衛尉陳球為司空。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Minister of Works Liu Yi was dismissed; Commandant of the Guards Chen Qiu was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Minister of Works Liu Yi was dismissed, and Commandant of the Guards Chen Qiu was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，帝好文學，自造《皇羲篇》五十章，因引諸生能為文賦者並待制鴻都門下。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor loved literature, himself composed fifty chapters of the "Imperial Xi" text, and therefore summoned scholars able to write prose and fu, all to await appointment at the Hongdu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor loved literature, composed fifty chapters of the "Imperial Xi" text himself, and summoned scholars skilled in prose and fu to await appointment at the Hongdu Gate.

sentences.zh: 後諸為尺牘及工書鳥篆者，皆加引召，遂至數十人。

translations.literal: Later all who wrote documents and were skilled in calligraphy and bird-and-seal script were also summoned, until they reached several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Later all skilled in documents, calligraphy, and seal script were also summoned, until they numbered several dozen.

sentences.zh: 侍中祭酒樂松、賈護多引無行趣勢之徒置其間，熹陳閭裡小事；

translations.literal: Libationer of the Attendants-in-Ordinary Yue Song and Jia Hu often introduced men of no conduct who curried power and placed them among the group, delighting in reporting petty neighborhood matters;
translations.idiomatic: Libationers Yue Song and Jia Hu often introduced men of no character who curried favor and power, delighting in reporting petty neighborhood gossip;

sentences.zh: 帝甚悅之，待以不次之位；

translations.literal: the emperor was greatly pleased and treated them with extraordinary appointments;
translations.idiomatic: the emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded them with extraordinary promotions;

sentences.zh: 又久不親行郊廟之禮。

translations.literal: he also long failed personally to perform the suburban and temple rites.
translations.idiomatic: he also long neglected to perform the suburban and temple sacrifices in person.

sentences.zh: 會詔群臣各陳政要，蔡邕上封事曰：「夫迎氣五郊，清廟祭祀，養老辟雍，皆帝者之大業，祖宗所祗奉也。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered the ministers each to set forth essential policies, Cai Yong submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Receiving the qi at the five suburbs, sacrifices in the Pure Temple, honoring the aged at the Piyong—all are the great enterprises of an emperor, what ancestors reverently upheld.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered ministers to set forth essential policies, Cai Yong submitted a sealed memorial: "Receiving the seasonal qi at the five suburbs, sacrifices in the Pure Temple, honoring the aged at the Piyong—these are the great enterprises of an emperor, what ancestors reverently upheld.

sentences.zh: 而有司數以蕃國疏喪、宮內產生及吏卒小污，廢闕不行，忘禮敬之大，任禁忌之書，拘信小故，以虧大典。

translations.literal: Yet the responsible officials repeatedly cite distant states' mourning notices, births within the palace, and minor defilements of clerks and soldiers to suspend and omit performance, forgetting the greatness of ritual reverence, trusting books of taboos, clinging to petty causes, and thereby impairing great ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials repeatedly cite distant states' mourning, births within the palace, and minor defilements of clerks and soldiers to suspend these rites, forgetting the greatness of ritual reverence, trusting books of taboos, clinging to petty causes, and thereby impairing great ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 自今齋制宜如故典，庶答風霆、災妖之異。

translations.literal: From now on fasting regulations should follow the old canon, that perhaps wind, thunder, and omens of disaster and anomaly may be answered.
translations.idiomatic: From now on fasting regulations should follow the old canon, that wind, thunder, and omens of disaster may be answered.

sentences.zh: 又，古者取士必使諸侯歲貢。

translations.literal: Moreover, in antiquity in selecting scholars the feudal lords were required to present annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in antiquity scholars were selected through annual tribute presentations by the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 孝武之世，郡舉孝廉，又有賢良、文學之選，於是名臣輩出，文武並興。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Wu, commanderies recommended Filial and Incorrupt men, and there were also selections of Worthy and Good and of Literary Learning; thus famous ministers emerged in succession, civil and military flourishing together.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu, commanderies recommended Filial and Incorrupt men, and Worthy and Good and Literary Learning selections were also held; thus famous ministers emerged in succession, and civil and military talent flourished together.

sentences.zh: 漢之得人，數路而已。

translations.literal: Han obtained its men through only a few routes.
translations.idiomatic: Han obtained its men through only a few established routes.

sentences.zh: 夫書畫辭賦，才之小者；

translations.literal: Painting, calligraphy, and literary compositions are minor talents;
translations.idiomatic: Painting, calligraphy, and literary compositions are minor talents;

sentences.zh: 匡國治政，未有其能。

translations.literal: in ordering the state and governing affairs they have no such ability.
translations.idiomatic: they have no ability to order the state and govern affairs.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位之初，先涉經術，聽政餘日，觀省篇章，聊以游意當代博奕，非以為教化取士之本。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, you first engaged with classical learning; on days left from hearing affairs you reviewed texts, merely to divert the mind with contemporary diversions—not taking this as the foundation of education and selection of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, you engaged with classical learning; on days left from affairs of state you reviewed texts, merely as diversion—not as the foundation of education and official selection.

sentences.zh: 而諸生競利，作者鼎沸，其高者頗引經訓風喻之言，下則連偶俗語，有類徘優，或竊成文，虛冒名氏。

translations.literal: Yet the scholars compete for profit, authors seethe like a cauldron; the higher sort somewhat cite canonical instruction and admonitory phrasing, the lower link vulgar couplets like jesters, some steal finished compositions and falsely claim authorship.
translations.idiomatic: Yet scholars compete for profit and authors swarm like a cauldron. The better sort cite canonical instruction; the worse link vulgar couplets like jesters, some steal finished works and falsely claim authorship.

sentences.zh: 臣每受詔於盛化門，差次錄第，其未及者，亦復隨輩皆見拜擢。

translations.literal: Your servant each time received edicts at the Shenghua Gate, ranked and recorded grades; those who did not qualify were also promoted along with the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I received edicts at the Shenghua Gate to rank candidates; even those who did not qualify were promoted along with the rest.

sentences.zh: 既加之恩，難復收改，但守奉祿，於義已弘，不可復使治民及在州郡。

translations.literal: Once favor has been granted, it is hard to withdraw; let them only hold salaries—in generosity this is already ample; they must not again be made to govern the people or serve in provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Once favor is granted, it is hard to withdraw; let them hold salaries only—that is already generous enough. They must not be made to govern the people or serve in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 昔孝宣會諸儒於石渠，章帝集學士於白虎，通經釋義，其事優大，文武之道，所宜從之。

translations.literal: In the past Emperor Xuan gathered the ru at Shiqu, Emperor Zhang assembled scholars at Baihu—expounding the classics and explaining meaning, matters of eminent greatness; the way of civil and military affairs is what one should follow.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan once gathered scholars at Shiqu; Emperor Zhang assembled them at Baihu to expound the classics—matters of eminent greatness. The way of civil and military affairs is what Your Majesty should follow.

sentences.zh: 若乃不能小善，雖有可觀，孔子以為致遠則泥，君子固當志其大者。

translations.literal: If one cannot achieve small goodness, though there is something to view, Confucius held that for reaching far it becomes obstructive—a gentleman should fix his aim on the greater matters.
translations.idiomatic: If one lacks even small virtues, though there may be something to admire, Confucius held that for reaching far it becomes obstructive. A gentleman should fix his aim on greater matters.

sentences.zh: 又，前一切以宣陵孝子為太子舍人，臣聞孝文皇帝制喪服三十六日，雖繼體之君，父子至親，公卿列臣受恩之重，皆屈情從制，不敢逾越。

translations.literal: Moreover, earlier all the filial sons of Xuanling were made Attendants of the Heir Apparent. Your servant has heard that Emperor Wen regulated mourning garments for thirty-six days; though a successor sovereign, father and son most intimate, the excellencies and ranked ministers receiving heavy grace—all bent feeling to follow the regulation and dared not transgress.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, all the so-called filial sons of Xuanling were made Attendants of the Heir Apparent. I have heard that Emperor Wen regulated mourning for thirty-six days; though a successor sovereign is father and son most intimate, and the excellencies received heavy grace—all bent feeling to the regulation and dared not transgress.

sentences.zh: 今虛偽小人，本非骨肉，既無幸私之恩，又無祿仕之實，惻隱之心，義無所依，至有奸軌之人通容其中。

translations.literal: Now these false petty men are not kin by blood; they have neither the grace of private favor nor the substance of salary and office; compassionate feeling has no ground in righteousness—and even wicked schemers find shelter among them.
translations.idiomatic: Now these false petty men are not kin by blood; they have neither private favor nor salary and office; their show of compassion has no ground in righteousness—and even wicked schemers find shelter among them.

sentences.zh: 桓思皇后祖載之時，東郡有盜人妻者，亡在孝中，本縣追捕，乃伏其辜。

translations.literal: When Empress Huansi's ancestral carriage departed, in Dong Commandery a man who had stolen another's wife hid himself in mourning; the native county pursued and arrested him, and he confessed his crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Huansi's funeral procession departed, in Dong Commandery a man who had stolen another's wife hid himself among the mourners; the county pursued and arrested him, and he confessed his crime.

sentences.zh: 虛偽雜穢，難得勝言。

translations.literal: Falsehood and filth mixed together—hard to exhaust in words.
translations.idiomatic: The falsehood and filth are beyond full description.

sentences.zh: 太子官屬，宜搜選令德，豈有但取丘墓凶丑之人！

translations.literal: The heir's officials should be sought and selected for fine virtue—how can one merely take men of tombs, inauspicious and vile!
translations.idiomatic: The heir's officials should be sought for fine virtue—how can one merely take men who lurk at tombs, inauspicious and vile!

sentences.zh: 其為不祥，莫與大焉，宜遣歸田裡，以明詐偽。

translations.literal: Nothing could be more inauspicious; they should be sent back to their villages to make clear the fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing could be more inauspicious; they should be sent back to their villages to expose the fraud.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，帝乃親迎氣北郊及行辟雍之禮。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor then personally received the qi at the northern suburb and performed the Piyong rites.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor personally received the seasonal qi at the northern suburb and performed the Piyong rites.

sentences.zh: 又詔宣陵孝子為舍人者悉改為丞、尉焉。

translations.literal: He also ordered that all filial sons of Xuanling who had been made Attendants be changed to assistants and commandants.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered that all so-called filial sons of Xuanling appointed as Attendants be reassigned as assistants and commandants.

sentences.zh: 護烏桓校尉夏育上言：「鮮卑寇邊，自春以來三十餘發，請征幽州諸郡兵出塞擊之，一冬、二春，必能禽滅。

translations.literal: Colonel Protector of the Wuhuan Xia Yu submitted a statement: "The Xianbei raid the borders; since spring there have been more than thirty incursions. I request mobilizing the troops of You Province's commanderies to go beyond the passes and strike them; in one winter and two springs they can surely be captured and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Protector of the Wuhuan Xia Yu submitted a statement: "The Xianbei have raided the borders more than thirty times since spring. I request mobilizing the troops of You Province to strike beyond the passes; in one winter and two springs they can surely be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 」先是護羌校尉田晏坐事論刑，被原，欲立功自效，乃請中常侍王甫求得為將。

translations.literal: " Earlier Colonel Protector of the Qiang Tian Yan had been sentenced for an offense, was pardoned, wished to establish merit to redeem himself, and therefore asked the Regular Palace Attendant Wang Fu to obtain appointment as a general.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier Colonel Protector of the Qiang Tian Yan had been sentenced for an offense, pardoned, and wished to redeem himself through merit. He asked the palace attendant Wang Fu to obtain a general's command for him.

sentences.zh: 甫因此議遣兵與育並力討賊，帝乃拜晏為破鮮卑中郎將；

translations.literal: Fu therefore urged dispatching troops to join Yu in attacking the bandits; the emperor then appointed Yan General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household Who Breaks the Xianbei;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu therefore urged dispatching troops to join Yu in suppressing the raiders, and the emperor appointed Yan General Who Breaks the Xianbei;

sentences.zh: 大臣多有不同，乃召百官議於朝堂。

translations.literal: many ministers differed, and the emperor summoned the hundred officials to deliberate in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: many ministers objected, and the emperor summoned the officials to deliberate in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕議曰：「征討殊類，所由尚矣。

translations.literal: Cai Yong argued: "Campaigns against foreign peoples have long been esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong argued: "Campaigns against foreign peoples have long been undertaken.

sentences.zh: 然而時有同異，勢有可否，故謀有得失，事有成敗，不可齊也。

translations.literal: Yet times differ in agreement and opposition, circumstances differ in feasibility and impossibility; hence plans have gain and loss, affairs have success and failure—they cannot be made uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Yet times differ, circumstances differ in feasibility, plans have gain and loss, and affairs succeed or fail—they cannot be treated uniformly.

sentences.zh: 夫以世宗神武，將帥良猛，財賦充實，所括廣遠，數十年間，官民俱匱，猶有悔焉。

translations.literal: Even with Emperor Wu's divine martial prowess, generals good and fierce, revenues full and ample, and campaigns sweeping far and wide—for several decades officials and people alike were exhausted, and there was still regret.
translations.idiomatic: Even Emperor Wu, with divine martial prowess, excellent generals, and full revenues, campaigning far and wide for decades exhausted officials and people alike—and there was still regret.

sentences.zh: 況今人財並乏，事劣昔時乎！

translations.literal: How much more when men and wealth are both depleted and affairs are inferior to former times!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when men and wealth are both depleted and conditions inferior to former times!

sentences.zh: 自匈奴遁逃，鮮卑強盛，據其故地，稱兵十萬，才力勁健，意智益生；

translations.literal: Since the Xiongnu fled, the Xianbei have grown strong, occupied their old lands, field a hundred thousand armed men, their talent and strength vigorous, their wit and intelligence ever increasing;
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xiongnu fled, the Xianbei have grown strong, occupied their old lands, field a hundred thousand armed men, vigorous in talent and strength, ever increasing in wit and intelligence;

sentences.zh: 加以關塞不嚴，禁網多漏，精金良鐵，皆為賊有，漢人逋逃為之謀主，兵利馬疾，過於匈奴。

translations.literal: added to this, passes and barriers are not strict, prohibitions leak in many places, fine gold and good iron all fall to the bandits, Han fugitives serve as their strategists—their weapons sharp, horses swift, surpassing the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: passes and barriers are poorly guarded, prohibitions leak everywhere, fine metal falls to the raiders, Han fugitives serve as their strategists—their weapons sharp, horses swift, surpassing the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 昔段熲良將，習兵善戰，有事西羌，猶十餘年。

translations.literal: In the past Duan Yong was a fine general, practiced in arms and skilled in battle; campaigning against the Western Qiang still took more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yong was a fine general, practiced in arms and skilled in battle; campaigning against the Western Qiang still took more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 今育、晏才策未必過熲，鮮卑種眾不弱曩時，而虛計二載，自許有成，若禍結兵連，豈得中休？

translations.literal: Now Yu and Yan's talent and plans need not surpass Yong's; the Xianbei tribes and masses are not weaker than before—yet they recklessly plan two years and promise themselves success. If disaster binds and war continues, can it halt midway?
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Yan's talent need not surpass Yong's; the Xianbei are not weaker than before—yet they recklessly promise success in two years. If disaster binds and war continues, can it halt midway?

sentences.zh: 當復征發眾人，轉運無已，是為耗竭諸夏，並力蠻夷。

translations.literal: There will again be levies and mobilization of the masses, transport without end—this is to exhaust the Central States and join strength with the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: There will again be levies and mobilization, transport without end—exhausting the Central States to join strength with the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 夫邊垂之患，手足之疥搔，中國之困，胸背之瘭疽，方今郡縣盜賊尚不能禁，況此醜虜而可伏乎！

translations.literal: Border troubles are like itching scabs on the hands and feet; China's distress is like gangrene on chest and back. At present commandery and county bandits still cannot be suppressed—how much less can these vile barbarians be subdued!
translations.idiomatic: Border troubles are like itching scabs on the hands and feet; the empire's distress is like gangrene on chest and back. Commandery and county bandits still cannot be suppressed—how much less can these vile barbarians be subdued!

sentences.zh: 昔高祖忍平城之恥，呂後棄慢書之詬，方之於今，何者為甚？

translations.literal: In the past Gaozu endured the shame of Pingcheng; Empress Lü set aside the insult of the arrogant letter—compared with today, which is the greater?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu endured the shame of Pingcheng; Empress Lü set aside the insult of the arrogant letter—compared with today, which is the greater?

sentences.zh: 天設山河，秦築長城，漢起塞垣，所以別內外，異殊俗也。

translations.literal: Heaven set mountains and rivers; Qin built the Long Wall; Han raised frontier ramparts—to distinguish inner from outer and separate alien customs.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven set mountains and rivers; Qin built the Long Wall; Han raised frontier ramparts—to distinguish inner from outer and separate alien customs.

sentences.zh: 苟無蹙國內侮之患則可矣，豈與蟲蟻之虜，校往來之數哉！

translations.literal: If there is no peril of constricting the state or internal insult, that suffices—why reckon the tally of comings and goings with insect-and-ant barbarians!
translations.idiomatic: If there is no peril of constricting the state or internal disorder, that suffices—why reckon comings and goings with insect-and-ant barbarians!

sentences.zh: 雖或破之，豈可殄盡，而方令本朝為之旰食乎！

translations.literal: Even if they are sometimes defeated, can they be exterminated entirely—and should this court be made to lose sleep over them!
translations.idiomatic: Even if they are sometimes defeated, can they be exterminated entirely—and should this court lose sleep over them!

sentences.zh: 昔淮南王安諫伐越曰：『如使越人蒙死以逆執事，廝輿之卒有一不備而歸者，雖得越王之首，猶為大漢羞之。

translations.literal: In the past Huainan King Liu An remonstrated against attacking Yue, saying: "If the Yue people risk death to oppose your servants, and of the cart-driving soldiers even one returns unprepared, though you obtain the King of Yue's head, it will still be a shame to Great Han.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan King Liu An once remonstrated against attacking Yue: "If the Yue risk death to oppose your servants, and even one common soldier returns unprepared, though you obtain the King of Yue's head, it will still shame Great Han.

sentences.zh: 』而欲以齊民易丑虜，皇威辱外夷，就如其言，猶已危矣，況乎得失不可量邪！

translations.literal: Yet you wish to exchange orderly citizens for vile barbarians and to humiliate the imperial majesty before foreign tribes—even as his words describe, it is already perilous; how much more when gain and loss cannot be measured!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you would trade orderly subjects for vile barbarians and bring the imperial majesty to shame before foreign tribes—even on his account alone the risk is grave; how much worse when the outcome cannot be reckoned!

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to follow his advice.

sentences.zh: 八月，遣夏育出高柳，田晏出雲中，匈奴中郎將臧旻率南單于出雁門，各將萬騎，三道出塞二千餘里。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Xia Yu was sent out from Gaoliu, Tian Yan from Yunzhong, and the Xiongnu Commandant Zang Min led the Southern Chanyu out from Yanmen; each commanded ten thousand horsemen, and the three columns went beyond the frontier more than two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the court dispatched Xia Yu from Gaoliu, Tian Yan from Yunzhong, and Xiongnu Commandant Zang Min with the Southern Chanyu from Yanmen—each at the head of ten thousand cavalry—on three routes that penetrated more than two thousand li beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 檀石槐命三部大人各帥眾逆戰，育等大敗，喪其節傳輜重，各將數十騎奔還，死者什七八。

translations.literal: Tanshihuai ordered the three division chiefs each to lead their forces to meet them in battle; Yu and the others were utterly defeated, lost their credentials of office and baggage trains, and each fled back with only several dozen horsemen; seven or eight in ten of the dead perished.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshihuai ordered the chiefs of his three divisions each to lead their warriors against them. Yu and the others were routed, abandoning their insignia and supply trains, and each escaped with only a few dozen riders; seven or eight soldiers in ten were killed.

sentences.zh: 三將檻車征下獄，贖為庶人。

translations.literal: The three generals were summoned back in prisoner carts and cast into prison, then ransomed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: All three commanders were recalled in prisoner carts, thrown into jail, and then redeemed down to commoner rank.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day of the cycle guichou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the new moon of guichou, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 太尉劉寬免。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Liu Kuan was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Liu Kuan was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，京師地震。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, the capital region was shaken by an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinchou an earthquake struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月，司空陳球免。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Minister of Works Chen Qiu was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Minister of Works Chen Qiu was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲寅，以太常河南孟彧為太尉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day jiayin, the Minister of Ceremonies Meng Yu of Henan was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiayin, Minister of Ceremonies Meng Yu of Henan was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，司徒楊賜免。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Minister over the Masses Yang Ci was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Minister over the Masses Yang Ci was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 以太常陳耽為司空。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies Chen Dan was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Chen Dan was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 遼西太守甘陵趙苞到官，遣使迎母及妻子，垂當到郡；

translations.literal: Zhao Bao of Ganling, Administrator of Liaoxi, took up his post and sent envoys to welcome his mother and wife and children; they were on the verge of reaching the commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bao of Ganling, the new Administrator of Liaoxi, had sent messengers to bring his mother, wife, and children to join him; they were almost at the commandery seat when—

sentences.zh: 道經柳城，值鮮卑萬餘人入塞寇鈔，苞母及妻子遂為所劫質，載以擊郡。

translations.literal: on the road they passed through Liucheng, where more than ten thousand Xianbei had crossed the frontier to raid and plunder; Bao's mother and wife and children were seized as hostages and carried along to attack the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: on the road through Liucheng they met more than ten thousand Xianbei who had crossed the border to raid. Bao's mother, wife, and children were taken hostage and driven before the invaders as they struck at the commandery.

sentences.zh: 苞率騎二萬與賊對陳，賊出母以示苞，苞悲號，謂母曰：「為子無狀，欲以微祿奉養朝夕，不圖為母作禍，昔為母子，今為王臣，義不得顧私恩，毀忠節，唯當萬死，無以塞罪。

translations.literal: Bao led twenty thousand horsemen to face the bandits in battle array; the bandits brought out his mother to show him. Bao wailed in grief and said to his mother: "As a son I have been worthless, wishing only to support you day and night on a modest salary, never imagining I would bring disaster upon you. Once we were mother and son; now I am the king's minister. By duty I cannot heed private affection and ruin loyalty and integrity. I can only die ten thousand deaths and still not atone for my crime.
translations.idiomatic: Bao led twenty thousand cavalry to meet the enemy in battle. The raiders paraded his mother before him. He wept aloud and called to her: "I have been a worthless son, hoping only to support you on a modest official's pay—I never meant to bring you harm. We were mother and son; now I am the king's servant. Duty forbids me to favor private love and betray loyalty. I deserve ten thousand deaths and cannot expiate my guilt.

sentences.zh: 」母遙謂曰：「威豪，人各有命，何得相顧以虧忠義，爾其勉之！

translations.literal: From afar his mother called back: "Weihao, each person has his allotted fate—how can you look to me and thereby impair loyalty and righteousness? Press on!
translations.idiomatic: His mother shouted back from a distance: "Weihao! Each of us has his fate—do not look to me and sacrifice loyalty and righteousness. Do your duty!"

sentences.zh: 」苞即時進戰，賊悉摧破，其母妻皆為所害。

translations.literal: Bao at once pressed the attack; the bandits were all shattered and destroyed, but his mother and wife were both killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Bao immediately pressed the attack, shattered the enemy completely, and his mother and wife were slain in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 苞自上歸葬，帝遣使弔慰，封鄃侯。

translations.literal: Bao himself submitted a memorial requesting leave to bury them; the Emperor sent envoys to offer condolences and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Bao memorialized the throne for leave to bury them. The emperor sent envoys with condolences and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Ju.

sentences.zh: 苞葬訖，謂鄉人曰：「食祿而避難，非忠也；

translations.literal: When the burial was finished, he said to his fellow townspeople: "To draw a salary yet shrink from peril is not loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral he told his neighbors, "To take the state's pay yet flee from danger is not loyalty;

sentences.zh: 殺母以全義，非孝也。

translations.literal: to kill one's mother in order to preserve righteousness is not filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: to let one's mother die in order to preserve duty is not filial piety.

sentences.zh: 如是，有何面目立於天下！

translations.literal: Having done both, what face have I to stand beneath heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Having done both, what face have I to live among men!

sentences.zh: 」遂歐血而死。

translations.literal: He thereupon vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: He then vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，合浦、交趾烏滸蠻反，招引九真、日南民攻沒郡縣。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Wuhu barbarians of Hepu and Jiaozhi rebelled, drawing the people of Jiuzhen and Rinan to attack and overrun commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring the Wuhu tribes of Hepu and Jiaozhi rose in revolt, rallying the people of Jiuzhen and Rinan to overrun commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 太尉孟彧罷。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Meng Yu was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Meng Yu was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day of the cycle xinhai, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the new moon of xinhai, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以光祿勳陳國袁滂為司徒。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, the Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yuan Pang of Chen was appointed Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yuan Pang of Chen was made Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 己未，地震。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, there was an earthquake.
