translations.idiomatic: On jiwei an earthquake occurred.

sentences.zh: 置鴻都門學，其諸生皆敕州郡、三公舉用辟召，或出為刺史、太守，入為尚書、侍中，有封侯、賜爵者；

translations.literal: The Hongdu Gate Academy was established; its students were all ordered to be recommended and summoned by the provinces, commanderies, and the Three Excellencies; some went out as regional inspectors or grand administrators, some entered as Masters of Writing or Palace Attendants, and some received enfeoffment as marquises or bestowal of noble rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Hongdu Gate Academy was founded. Its students were recruited by imperial order through the provinces and the Three Excellencies; some were sent out as regional inspectors or grand administrators, others brought in as Masters of Writing or Palace Attendants, and some were enfeoffed or granted noble titles—

sentences.zh: 士君子皆恥與為列焉。

translations.literal: gentlemen and scholars all were ashamed to be ranked with them.
translations.idiomatic: and cultivated gentlemen were ashamed to be classed with them.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛丑，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day xinchou, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm and the reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinchou, the empire was granted a general amnesty and the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 以太常常山張顥為太尉。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Hao of Changshan was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Hao of Changshan was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 顥，中常侍奉之弟也。

translations.literal: Hao was the younger brother of the Regular Palace Attendant Zhang Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was the younger brother of Regular Palace Attendant Zhang Feng.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙辰，地震。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day bingchen, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on bingchen, an earthquake occurred.

sentences.zh: 侍中寺雌雞化為雄。

translations.literal: In the Palace Attendant's office a hen transformed into a rooster.
translations.idiomatic: At the Palace Attendant's office a hen turned into a rooster.

sentences.zh: 司空陳耽免；

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chen Dan was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chen Dan was removed from office;

sentences.zh: 以太常來艷為司空。

translations.literal: the Minister of Ceremonies Lai Yan was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: and Minister of Ceremonies Lai Yan was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁丑，有黑氣墮帝所御溫德殿東庭中，長十餘丈，似龍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day dingchou, black vapor fell into the eastern courtyard of the Wendé Hall where the Emperor resided; it was more than ten zhang long and resembled a dragon.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingchou, a black cloud-like mass fell into the eastern court of the Wendé Hall where the emperor dwelt; it stretched more than ten zhang and looked like a dragon.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬子，青虹見玉堂後殿庭中。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day renzi, a green rainbow appeared in the courtyard behind the Yutang Rear Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on renzi, a green rainbow appeared in the courtyard behind the Yutang Rear Hall.

sentences.zh: 詔召光祿大夫楊賜等詣金商門，問以災異及消復之術。

translations.literal: An edict summoned the Grand Masters of the Palace Yang Ci and others to the Jingshang Gate and questioned them on the portents and the means to dispel and restore order.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Grand Masters of the Palace Yang Ci and others to the Jingshang Gate to answer questions on the omens and how to avert calamity.

sentences.zh: 賜對曰：「《春秋言韱》曰：『天投蜺，天下怨，海內亂。

translations.literal: Yang Ci replied: "The Yan of the Spring and Autumn Annals says: 'When Heaven casts down the rainbow, all under Heaven resent it; within the seas there is disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ci answered, "The Yan commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says, 'When Heaven casts down the rainbow, the realm resents it and the empire falls into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 』加四百之期，亦復垂及。

translations.literal: Add the span of four hundred years, and that too is now nearly at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Add four hundred years, and that season too is almost upon us.

sentences.zh: 今妾媵、閹尹之徒共專國朝，欺罔日月；

translations.literal: Now concubines and eunuch chamberlains and the like together monopolize the court, deceiving and obscuring the sun and moon;
translations.idiomatic: Today concubines, eunuchs, and their kind monopolize the court and darken the sun and moon;

sentences.zh: 又，鴻都門下招會群小，造作賦說，見寵於時，更相薦說，旬月之間，並各拔擢。

translations.literal: moreover, under the Hongdu Gate petty men are gathered, composing fu and discourse, favored in their time, recommending one another in turn, and within a month or so all are promoted together.
translations.idiomatic: and under the Hongdu Gate petty men are assembled to write fu and essays, winning favor and promoting one another until within weeks they are all advanced.

sentences.zh: 樂松處常伯，任芝居納言，郤儉、梁鵠各受豐爵不次之寵，而令搢紳之徒委伏畎畝，口誦堯、舜之言，身蹈絕俗之行，棄捐溝壑，不見逮及。

translations.literal: Yue Song holds the rank of Regular Grand Master, Ren Zhi occupies the post of Grand Master of Speech, Xi Jian and Liang Hu each receive rich enfeoffments and extraordinary favor, while gentry in official silks are made to lie prostrate in the fields, reciting the words of Yao and Shun yet practicing conduct beyond the vulgar, cast away in ditches and gullies, never brought forward.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Song holds a chief-counselor's rank, Ren Zhi a censor's post; Xi Jian and Liang Hu enjoy lavish titles and unmerited favor, while true gentlemen are left prostrate in the fields—chanting Yao and Shun yet living in utter integrity—abandoned in obscurity and never advanced.

sentences.zh: 冠履倒易，陵谷代處，幸賴皇天垂象譴告。

translations.literal: Cap and shoe are reversed, hill and valley change places—fortunately we rely on August Heaven's hanging forth of signs in reproof and warning.
translations.idiomatic: Hats and shoes are reversed, high and low exchanged—fortunately August Heaven has sent omens of warning.

sentences.zh: 《周書》曰：『天子見怪則修德，諸侯見怪則修政，卿大夫見怪則修職，士庶人見怪則修身。

translations.literal: The Book of Zhou says: 'When the Son of Heaven sees a prodigy he cultivates virtue; when feudal lords see a prodigy they rectify government; when ministers and grandees see a prodigy they rectify their duties; when gentlemen and commoners see a prodigy they cultivate the person.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Zhou says, 'When the Son of Heaven sees a portent he cultivates virtue; when feudal lords see one they reform government; when ministers see one they reform their offices; when commoners see one they reform themselves.

sentences.zh: 』唯陛下斥遠佞巧之臣，速征鶴鳴之士，斷絕尺一，抑止槃游，冀上天還威，眾變可弭！

translations.literal: May Your Majesty alone drive far away crafty flatterers, swiftly summon men whose call is like the crane's cry, cut off the inch-wide edicts, and restrain roaming and sport—hoping that Heaven will restore its majesty and the multitude of changes may be quelled!
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty banish crafty flatterers, swiftly summon worthy men of hidden virtue, cease issuing petty edicts, and curb idle roaming—so that Heaven may restore its authority and these many portents be stilled!

sentences.zh: 議郎蔡邕對曰：「臣伏思諸異，皆亡國之怪也。

translations.literal: Consulting Gentleman Cai Yong replied: "Your servant has pondered all these prodigies; they are all monsters presaging a state's ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Consulting Gentleman Cai Yong answered, "I have considered these omens carefully—they are all portents of a state's fall.

sentences.zh: 天於大漢殷勤不已，故屢出祅變以當譴責，欲令人君感悟，改危即安。

translations.literal: Heaven toward Great Han has been unceasingly attentive, and therefore repeatedly sends demonic transformations in place of reproof, wishing to make the ruler awaken and turn peril into peace.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has shown Great Han unceasing care, sending repeated uncanny signs as warnings so that the sovereign may awaken and turn danger into safety.

sentences.zh: 今蜺墮、雞化，皆婦人干政之所致也。

translations.literal: Now the falling of the rainbow and the hen's transformation are all brought about by women's interference in government.
translations.idiomatic: The fallen rainbow and the hen turned rooster all stem from women meddling in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 前者乳母趙嬈，貴重天下，讒諛驕溢，續以永樂門史霍玉，依阻城社，又為奸邪。

translations.literal: Earlier the wet nurse Zhao Rao was honored above all the realm, slander and flattery overflowing in arrogance; this was followed by Huo Yu, clerk of the Yongle Gate, relying on walls and altars of earth as his support, again acting as a wicked traitor.
translations.idiomatic: First the wet nurse Zhao Rao held sway over the realm, her slander and flattery swollen with arrogance; then Huo Yu, clerk of the Yongle Gate, leaned on factional power and again did evil.

sentences.zh: 今道路紛紛，復雲有程大人者，察其風聲，將為國患；

translations.literal: Now the roads are abuzz, and again it is said there is a Lord Cheng; judging from the rumors, he will become a calamity to the state;
translations.idiomatic: Now the streets are full of talk of a 'Lord Cheng'; from the rumors abroad he will become a scourge to the state—

sentences.zh: 宜高為堤防，明設禁令，深惟趙、霍，以為至戒。

translations.literal: one ought to raise high dikes and defenses, clearly set forth prohibitions, and deeply take Zhao and Huo as the supreme warning.
translations.idiomatic: you should raise high barriers, set clear prohibitions, and take Zhao and Huo as the gravest warning.

sentences.zh: 今太尉張顥，為玉所進；

translations.literal: Now Grand Commandant Zhang Hao was advanced by Yu;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Zhang Hao was promoted by Huo Yu;

sentences.zh: 光祿勳偉璋，有名貪濁；

translations.literal: the Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wei Zhang is notorious for greed and corruption;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wei Zhang is notorious for greed and corruption;

sentences.zh: 又長水校尉趙玹，屯騎校尉蓋升，並叨時幸，榮富優足；

translations.literal: also Commandant of the Changshui Garrison Zhao Xuan and Commandant of the Tunqi Garrison Gai Sheng both enjoy the favor of the times, their glory and wealth abundant;
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the Changshui Garrison Zhao Xuan and Commandant of the Tunqi Garrison Gai Sheng likewise enjoy the court's favor and live in lavish ease—

sentences.zh: 宜念小人在位之咎，退思引身避賢之福。

translations.literal: they ought to reflect on the fault of petty men holding office and, in retiring, consider the blessing of withdrawing the body to yield place to the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: they should reflect on the guilt of unworthy men in high place and consider the blessing of stepping aside for the worthy.

sentences.zh: 伏見廷尉郭禧，純厚老成；

translations.literal: Your servant has observed Court Commandant Guo Xi—pure, thick, and seasoned with age;
translations.idiomatic: I observe Court Commandant Guo Xi—sincere, steadfast, and experienced;

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫橋玄，聰達方直；

translations.literal: Grand Master of the Palace Qiao Xuan—perceptive, penetrating, upright and square;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of the Palace Qiao Xuan—wise, forthright, and upright;

sentences.zh: 故太尉劉寵，忠實守正；

translations.literal: former Grand Commandant Liu Chong—loyal, solid, and holding to the right;
translations.idiomatic: former Grand Commandant Liu Chong—loyal, steadfast, and upright—

sentences.zh: 並宜為謀主，數見訪問。

translations.literal: all ought to serve as masters of counsel and be repeatedly consulted.
translations.idiomatic: all should serve as your chief advisers and be consulted often.

sentences.zh: 夫宰相大臣，君之四體，委任責成，優劣已分，不宜聽納小吏，雕琢大臣也，又，尚方工技之作，鴻都篇賦之文，可且消息，以示惟優。

translations.literal: Chancellors and great ministers are the ruler's four limbs; once entrusted with responsibility for results, superior and inferior are already distinguished—one should not listen to and accept petty clerks who carve and polish the great ministers. Moreover, the craftworks of the Imperial Workshop and the fu compositions of Hongdu may for the time be suspended, to show concern only for what is essential.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors and ministers are the sovereign's four limbs: once entrusted with full responsibility, their merit is clear, and petty clerks should not be allowed to meddle with and reshape them. The Imperial Workshop's crafts and Hongdu's literary compositions might also be suspended for now, showing that the court cares only for essentials.

sentences.zh: 宰府孝廉，士之高選，近者以辟召不慎，切責三公，而今並以小文超取選舉，開請托之門，違明王之黃，眾心不厭，莫之敢言。

translations.literal: Filial and Incorrupt candidates from the chancellor's offices are the highest selection of gentlemen; recently because summons were not careful the Three Excellencies were sharply rebuked, yet now all are advanced in selection by petty compositions, opening the gate of private entreaty, violating the enlightened king's standard, and though the hearts of the multitude are displeased, none dares speak.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and Incorrupt nominees are the highest class of scholar-officials; the Three Excellencies were recently rebuked for careless summons, yet now men are promoted on trifling essays, opening the door to patronage and violating the enlightened king's standard. The people are disgusted, but none dare speak.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下忍而絕之，思惟萬機，以答天望。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to bear with it and cut it off, ponder the myriad affairs of state, and answer Heaven's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to endure this and cut it off, ponder the myriad affairs of state, and answer Heaven's hope.

sentences.zh: 聖朝既自約厲，左右近臣亦宜從化，人自抑損，以塞咎戒，則天道虧滿，鬼神福謙矣。

translations.literal: Since the sacred court has already restrained itself, attendants left and right should also follow in transformation; let each man restrain and diminish himself to block fault and warning—then the Way of Heaven will diminish the full, and ghosts and spirits will bless the humble.
translations.idiomatic: Since the court has already disciplined itself, those close to the throne should follow suit; let each restrain himself to ward off reproof, and Heaven's way will trim the proud while spirits bless the humble.

sentences.zh: 夫君臣不密，上有漏言之戒，下有失身之禍，願寢臣表，無使盡忠之吏受怨奸仇。

translations.literal: When ruler and minister are not discreet, above there is the warning against leaking words, below the calamity of losing one's person; I wish Your Majesty to suppress my memorial and not let officials who exhaust loyalty suffer resentment from wicked enemies.
translations.idiomatic: When ruler and minister are not discreet, the court warns against leaks above while servants risk ruin below. I beg Your Majesty to suppress my memorial so that loyal officials need not suffer the hatred of wicked foes.

sentences.zh: 」章奏，帝覽而歎息。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor read it and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor read it and sighed.

sentences.zh: 因起更衣，曹節於後竊視之，悉宣語左右，事遂漏露。

translations.literal: He then rose to change garments; Cao Jie behind him stole a look and fully proclaimed its words to those at his side, and the matter was thus leaked.
translations.idiomatic: He then rose to change clothes; Cao Jie peeked from behind and repeated the whole memorial to those beside him, and the affair was leaked.

sentences.zh: 其為邕所裁黜者，側目思報。

translations.literal: Those whom Yong had censured and demoted glared sidelong, thinking how to retaliate.
translations.idiomatic: Those whom Yong had criticized glared at him sideways, plotting revenge.

sentences.zh: 初，邕與大鴻臚劉命素不相平，叔父衛尉質又與將作大匠陽球有隙。

translations.literal: Earlier Yong and the Grand Herald Liu Ming had long been on bad terms, and his uncle the Commandant of the Guards Zhi also had a rift with the Master of Works Yang Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yong had long been at odds with Grand Herald Liu Ming, and his uncle Commandant of the Guards Zhi also bore a grudge against Master of Works Yang Qiu.

sentences.zh: 球即中常侍程璜女夫也。

translations.literal: Qiu was the son-in-law of the Regular Palace Attendant Cheng Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was the son-in-law of Regular Palace Attendant Cheng Huang.

sentences.zh: 璜遂使人飛章言「邕、質數以私事請托於郃，郃不聽。

translations.literal: Huang then had someone send a flying memorial saying: "Yong and Zhi repeatedly entreated He on private matters, and He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Huang then had a secret memorial sent alleging, "Yong and Zhi repeatedly asked Liu He for private favors, and He refused.

sentences.zh: 邕含隱切，志欲相中。

translations.literal: Yong harbored hidden resentment and was bent on striking He down.
translations.idiomatic: Yong nursed secret hatred and meant to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 」於中詔下尚書召邕詰狀。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict from within ordered the Masters of Writing to summon Yong and question him on the charges.
translations.idiomatic: An edict from within ordered the Masters of Writing to summon Yong and examine the charges.

sentences.zh: 邕上書曰：「臣實愚戇，不顧後害，陛下不念忠臣直言，宜加掩蔽，誹謗卒至，便用疑怪。

translations.literal: Yong submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant is truly stupid and blunt, heedless of later harm. Your Majesty did not consider the loyal minister's straight words and ought to have covered them over; slander suddenly arrived, and you at once grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Yong submitted a memorial: "I was foolish and blunt, heedless of consequences. Your Majesty did not shield a loyal minister's frank words; slander came at once, and you grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 臣年四十有六，孤特一身，得托名忠臣，死有餘榮，恐陛下於此不復聞至言矣！

translations.literal: Your servant is forty-six years old, alone and solitary in one person; to be able to leave a name as a loyal minister, death would still leave surplus glory. I fear that from this Your Majesty will no longer hear utmost words!
translations.idiomatic: I am forty-six, alone in the world; if I may die with the name of loyal minister, I shall have honor enough. I fear Your Majesty will never again hear such frank counsel!"

sentences.zh: 」於是下邕、質於雒陽獄，劾以「仇怨奉公，議害大臣，大不敬，棄市。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yong and Zhi were cast into the Luoyang prison, impeached on the charge: "Serving the public out of private enmity, plotting harm to great ministers—greatest irreverence, execution in the marketplace."
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Zhi were then thrown into Luoyang prison on the charge of "using public office to settle private scores and plotting against great ministers—capital irreverence, death by dismemberment in the marketplace."

sentences.zh: 」事奏，中常侍河南呂強愍邕無罪，力為伸請。

translations.literal: When the case was reported, the Regular Palace Attendant Lü Qiang of Henan pitied Yong as guiltless and strove to plead on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was reported, Regular Palace Attendant Lü Qiang of Henan, believing Yong innocent, pleaded vigorously for him.

sentences.zh: 帝亦更思其章，有詔：「減死一等，與家屬髡金甘，徙朔鉗方，不得以赦令除。

translations.literal: The Emperor also reconsidered his memorial and issued an edict: "Reduce death by one degree; with his household shave the head and exile to the frontier of Shuofang, not to be removed by any amnesty edict."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also reconsidered his memorial and decreed: "Commute death by one degree; shave him and his family and exile them to Shuofang, never to be pardoned by amnesty."

sentences.zh: 」陽球使客追路刺邕，客感其義，皆莫為用。

translations.literal: Yang Qiu sent retainers to pursue him on the road and assassinate Yong; the retainers were moved by his righteousness and none would act.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiu sent agents to pursue and assassinate Yong on the road; moved by his integrity, none would do it.

sentences.zh: 球又賂其部主，使加毒害，所賂者反以其情戒邕，由是得免。

translations.literal: Qiu again bribed his escort chief to add poison; the man bribed instead warned Yong of the plot, and thereby he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu also bribed the escort chief to poison him; the bribed man instead warned Yong, and so he escaped.

sentences.zh: 八月，有星孛於天市。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, a broom star appeared in the Celestial Market.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month a comet appeared in the Celestial Market constellation.

sentences.zh: 九月，太尉張顥罷，以太常陳球為太尉。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Grand Commandant Zhang Hao was dismissed, and the Minister of Ceremonies Chen Qiu was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Grand Commandant Zhang Hao was removed, and Minister of Ceremonies Chen Qiu was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 司空來艷薨。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Lai Yan died.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Lai Yan died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，以屯騎校尉袁逢為司空。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Commandant of the Tunqi Garrison Yuan Feng was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Commandant of the Tunqi Garrison Yuan Feng was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 宋皇后無寵，後宮幸姬眾共譖毀。

translations.literal: Empress Song had no favor; the favored concubines of the inner palace together slandered and ruined her.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Song had fallen from favor, and the emperor's favored concubines joined in slandering her.

sentences.zh: 渤海王悝妃宋氏，即後之姑也，中常侍王甫恐後怨之，因譖後挾左道祝詛；

translations.literal: Lady Song, consort of Prince Kui of Bohai, was the empress's paternal aunt; the Regular Palace Attendant Wang Fu feared the empress would resent him and therefore slandered her as practicing heterodox ways and cursing by incantation;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Song, consort of Prince Kui of Bohai, was the empress's aunt. Regular Palace Attendant Wang Fu, fearing her resentment, slandered the empress for witchcraft and curses—

sentences.zh: 帝信之，遂策收璽綬。

translations.literal: the Emperor believed it and thereupon by edict seized back her seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor believed it and issued an edict stripping her of seal and sash.

sentences.zh: 後自致暴室，以憂死。

translations.literal: The empress herself entered the harsh chamber and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was confined to the harsh chamber and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 父不其鄉侯酆及兄弟並被誅。

translations.literal: Her father Feng, Marquis of the Village of Buqi, and her brothers were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Feng, Marquis of Buqi village, and her brothers were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 丙子晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On the last day of the cycle bingzi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of bingzi the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 尚書盧植上言：「凡諸黨錮多非其罪，可加赦恕，申宥回枉。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Lu Zhi submitted a memorial saying: "Of all those proscribed in the partisan cases, most are not guilty of their crimes; they may be granted pardon and forgiveness, extending grace to reverse wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Lu Zhi memorialized, "Most of those proscribed in the partisan purges were innocent; they should be pardoned and their wrongs redressed.

sentences.zh: 又，宋後家屬並以無辜委骸橫屍，不得斂葬，宜敕收拾，以安遊魂。

translations.literal: Moreover, the empress Song's kin were all, though guiltless, left as abandoned corpses lying across the land, unable to be gathered for burial; an order should be issued to collect and bury them, to settle their wandering souls.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Empress Song's kin lie slaughtered though innocent, unburied; order their remains collected so their spirits may rest.

sentences.zh: 又，郡守、刺史一月數遷，宜依黜陟以章能否，縱不九載，可滿三歲。

translations.literal: Moreover, grand administrators and regional inspectors are transferred several times in a month; one should follow promotion and demotion to display ability and inability—even if not the full nine years, three years would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, prefects and inspectors are rotated every few weeks; promotions and demotions should reflect merit—even if not the full nine-year term, three years would do.

sentences.zh: 又，請謁希求，一宜禁塞，選舉之事，責成主者。

translations.literal: Moreover, private petitions and eager seeking should all be forbidden and blocked; in matters of selection and recommendation, responsibility should be fixed on the presiding officer.
translations.idiomatic: Private petitions and favor-seeking should be wholly forbidden, and responsibility for nominations should rest with those in charge.

sentences.zh: 又，天子之體，理無私積，宜弘大務，蠲略細微。

translations.literal: Moreover, the person of the Son of Heaven by principle has no private hoarding; great affairs should be enlarged, and minutiae waived.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Son of Heaven should have no private hoard; he should attend to great affairs and set aside trifles.

sentences.zh: 」帝不省。

translations.literal: The Emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，太尉陳球免。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Grand Commandant Chen Qiu was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Grand Commandant Chen Qiu was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁巳，以光祿大夫橋玄為太尉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day dingsi, Grand Master of the Palace Qiao Xuan was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingsi, Grand Master of the Palace Qiao Xuan was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑寇酒泉；

translations.literal: The Xianbei raided Jiuquan;
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei raided Jiuquan;

sentences.zh: 種眾日多，緣邊莫不被毒。

translations.literal: their tribes grew daily in number, and along the frontier none escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: their numbers grew daily, and nowhere along the frontier was spared their ravages.

sentences.zh: 詔中尚方為鴻都文學樂松、江覽等三十二人圖像立贊，以勸學者。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Imperial Workshop to paint portraits and compose encomia for thirty-two men of Hongdu literary studies, including Yue Song and Jiang Lan, to encourage scholars.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Imperial Workshop to paint portraits and write encomia for thirty-two Hongdu scholars, including Yue Song and Jiang Lan, to encourage learning.

sentences.zh: 尚書令陽球諫曰：「臣案松、覽等皆出於微蔑，斗筲小人，依憑世戚，附托權豪，俛眉承睫，徼進明時。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Yang Qiu remonstrated: "Your servant finds that Song, Lan, and the rest all spring from the most contemptible origins—petty men of a peck and dipper measure, relying on kin of their generation, clinging to powerful magnates, bowing brows and receiving lashes of the eye, scheming to advance in this enlightened age.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Yang Qiu remonstrated, "I find that Song, Lan, and the rest come from the lowest origins—petty men who lean on powerful kin, fawn on the mighty, and scheme for office in this enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 或獻賦一篇，或鳥篆盈簡，而位升郎中，形圖丹青。

translations.literal: Some submit a single fu, some fill bamboo slips with bird-script seal characters, yet their rank rises to Gentleman of the Palace, and their forms are painted in cinnabar and green.
translations.idiomatic: Some offer a single fu, others fill scrolls with ornamental script, yet they rise to Gentleman of the Palace and have their portraits painted in brilliant colors.

sentences.zh: 亦有筆不點牘，辭不辨心，假手請字，妖偽百品，莫不被蒙殊恩，蟬蛻滓濁。

translations.literal: There are also those whose brush never touches the document, whose words cannot distinguish the mind, who borrow hands to beg for characters—a hundred sorts of demonic fraud, none failing to be clothed in extraordinary favor, casting off the sludge like cicadas.
translations.idiomatic: Some never touch brush to paper themselves, cannot compose their own words, and hire ghostwriters—a hundred kinds of fraud—all showered with extraordinary favor and lifted from the mire like cicadas from their shells.

sentences.zh: 是以有識掩口，天下嗟歎。

translations.literal: Therefore the knowing cover their mouths, and all under Heaven sigh in lament.
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment cover their mouths in shame, and the realm sighs in dismay.

sentences.zh: 臣聞圖像之設，以昭勸戒，欲令人君動鑒得失，未聞豎子小人詐作文頌，而可妄竊天官，垂象圖素者也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that portraits are established to display encouragement and warning, wishing to make the ruler moved to mirror gain and loss; I have never heard that boys and petty men who fraudulently compose essays and encomia may rashly usurp heavenly offices and hang their images on silk.
translations.idiomatic: Portraits are meant to teach and warn, moving the ruler to reflect on right and wrong. I have never heard that fraudulent essays by base men could justify usurping high office and hanging their likenesses on silk.

sentences.zh: 今太學、東觀足以宣明聖化，願罷鴻都之選，以銷天下之謗。

translations.literal: Now the Imperial Academy and the Eastern Pavilion suffice to proclaim and clarify sagely transformation; I wish to abolish the Hongdu selections, to dissolve the slander of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy and Eastern Pavilion already suffice to spread the sage's teaching. I beg you to abolish the Hongdu selections and silence the realm's reproach.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，不省。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it received no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 是歲，初開西邸賣官，入錢各有差；

translations.literal: That year, offices were first sold at the Western Lodge, with payments graded by rank;
translations.idiomatic: That year the court first opened the Western Lodge to sell offices, with fees set by rank—

sentences.zh: 二千石二千萬；

translations.literal: two-thousand-dan posts, twenty million;
translations.idiomatic: two-thousand-dan posts cost twenty million cash;

sentences.zh: 四百石四百萬；

translations.literal: four-hundred-dan posts, four million;
translations.idiomatic: four-hundred-dan posts, four million;

sentences.zh: 其以德次應選者半之，或三分之一；

translations.literal: for those selected by moral rank the fee was halved, or one-third;
translations.idiomatic: for candidates chosen on merit the fee was halved, or reduced to one-third;

sentences.zh: 於西園立庫以貯之。

translations.literal: a treasury was established in the Western Garden to store the proceeds.
translations.idiomatic: and a treasury was set up in the Western Garden to hold the payments.

sentences.zh: 或詣闕上書占令長，隨縣好醜，豐約有賈。

translations.literal: Some came to the palace gates and submitted memorials to reserve district magistracies; according to each county's desirability, prices were ample or modest.
translations.idiomatic: Some petitioned at court to reserve district magistracies, with prices varying by each county's desirability.

sentences.zh: 富者則先入錢，貧者到官然後倍輸。

translations.literal: The rich paid in advance; the poor paid double after taking office.
translations.idiomatic: The rich paid upfront; the poor paid double after assuming office.

sentences.zh: 又私令左右賣公卿，公千萬，卿五百萬。

translations.literal: He also privately ordered his attendants to sell the ranks of duke and minister—duke for ten million, minister for five million.
translations.idiomatic: He also secretly ordered his attendants to sell ducal and ministerial ranks—ten million for a duke, five million for a minister.

sentences.zh: 初，帝為侯時常苦貧，及即位，每歎桓帝不能作家居，曾無私錢，故賣官聚錢以為私藏。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor was a marquis he had often suffered poverty; upon ascending the throne he would sigh that Emperor Huan could not manage a household and had never a private coin—therefore he sold offices to amass money for a private hoard.
translations.idiomatic: As a marquis the emperor had known poverty; once enthroned he often lamented that Emperor Huan could not keep house and had no private funds—so he sold offices to build a personal treasury.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問侍中楊奇曰：「朕何如桓帝？

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked Palace Attendant Yang Qi: "How do I compare with Emperor Huan?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Palace Attendant Yang Qi, "How do I compare with Emperor Huan?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下之於桓帝，亦猶虞舜比德唐堯。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty compared with Emperor Huan is like Yu Shun matching virtue with Tang Yao.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your Majesty compared with Emperor Huan is like Yu Shun beside Tang Yao in virtue.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅曰：「卿強項，真楊震子孫，死後必復致大鳥矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor, displeased, said: "You are stiff-necked—truly a descendant of Yang Zhen; after death you will surely bring forth a great bird again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, displeased, said, "You are stiff-necked—a true descendant of Yang Zhen. After death you will surely hatch another great bird.

sentences.zh: 」奇，震之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Qi was Yang Zhen's great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was the great-grandson of Yang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 南匈奴屠特若屍逐就單于死，子呼征立。

translations.literal: The Southern Xiongnu Chanyu Tute Ruoshizhujiu died, and his son Huzheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Xiongnu Chanyu Tute Ruoshizhujiu died, and his son Huzheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 春，大疫。

translations.literal: In spring, a great pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: In spring a great pestilence swept the land.

sentences.zh: 三月，司徒袁滂免，以大鴻臚劉郃為司徒。

translations.literal: In the third month, Minister over the Masses Yuan Pang was dismissed, and Grand Herald Liu He was appointed Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Minister over the Masses Yuan Pang was removed, and Grand Herald Liu He was made Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，太尉橋玄罷，拜太中大夫；

translations.literal: On the day yichou, Grand Commandant Qiao Xuan was dismissed and appointed Grand Master of the Palace;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Grand Commandant Qiao Xuan was dismissed and appointed Grand Master of the Palace;

sentences.zh: 以太中大夫段熲為太尉。

translations.literal: Grand Master of the Palace Duan Yong was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of the Palace Duan Yong was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 玄幼子游門次，為人所劫，登樓求貨；

translations.literal: Xuan's young son was strolling at the gate when he was seized by robbers, who climbed a tower to demand ransom;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's young son was at the gate when bandits seized him, climbed a tower, and demanded ransom—

sentences.zh: 玄不與。

translations.literal: Xuan would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan refused.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉、河南尹圍守玄家，不敢迫。

translations.literal: The Commandant of the Metropolitan Area and the Intendant of Henan besieged Xuan's house but dared not press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Metropolitan Commandant and Intendant of Henan surrounded Xuan's house but dared not press the attack.

sentences.zh: 玄瞋目呼曰：「奸人無狀，玄豈以一子之命而縱國賊乎！

translations.literal: Xuan glared and shouted: "Wretches without shame—would Xuan spare the state's enemies for one son's life!
translations.idiomatic: Xuan glared and shouted, "Shameless villains—would I spare the state's enemies for one son's life!

sentences.zh: 」促令攻之，玄子亦死。

translations.literal: He urgently ordered the attack; Xuan's son also died.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered an immediate assault; his son died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 玄因上言：「天下凡有劫質，皆並殺之，不得贖以財寶，開張奸路。

translations.literal: Xuan thereupon submitted a memorial: "Throughout the realm, wherever there are hostages taken, kill them all together; do not ransom them with treasure, opening the way for villains.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan then memorialized, "Whenever hostages are taken anywhere in the realm, kill them all—never ransom them with treasure, lest we open the door to crime.

sentences.zh: 」由是劫質遂絕。

translations.literal: From this, hostage-taking ceased entirely.
translations.idiomatic: After that, hostage-taking largely ceased.

sentences.zh: 京兆地震。

translations.literal: The capital region was shaken by an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: An earthquake struck the capital region.

sentences.zh: 司空袁逢罷；

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yuan Feng was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yuan Feng was removed from office;

sentences.zh: 以太常張濟為司空。

translations.literal: the Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Ji was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: and Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Ji was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day of the cycle jiaxu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the new moon of jiaxu, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 王甫、曹節等奸虐弄權，扇動內外，太尉段熲阿附之。

translations.literal: Wang Fu, Cao Jie, and the rest were wicked and cruel, wielding power and stirring inner and outer courts; Grand Commandant Duan Yong fawned upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu, Cao Jie, and their faction were cruel and corrupt, manipulating power inside and outside the court; Grand Commandant Duan Yong curried their favor.

sentences.zh: 節、甫父兄子弟為卿、校、牧、守、令、長者佈滿天下，所在貪暴。

translations.literal: The fathers, elder and younger brothers, and sons of Jie and Fu as ministers, commandants, regional governors, grand administrators, magistrates, and chiefs were spread across all under Heaven, greedy and violent wherever they were.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Fu's kin filled the empire as ministers, commandants, governors, and magistrates, rapacious wherever they served.

sentences.zh: 甫養子吉為沛相，尤殘酷，凡殺人，皆磔屍車上，隨其罪目，宣示屬縣，夏月腐爛，則以繩連其骨，周遍一郡乃止，見者駭懼。

translations.literal: Fu's adopted son Ji was Administrator of Pei, especially cruel: for every person killed he dismembered the corpse on a cart, according to the crime's category posted it to the subordinate counties; in summer when the flesh rotted, he strung the bones on rope and toured the whole commandery before stopping—those who saw were struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's adopted son Ji, Administrator of Pei, was especially brutal: every execution was dismembered and displayed on carts throughout the commandery; in summer, when corpses rotted, he strung the bones on ropes and paraded them through the entire region—onlookers were horrified.

sentences.zh: 視事五年，凡殺萬餘人。

translations.literal: In five years of office he killed more than ten thousand persons in all.
translations.idiomatic: In five years in office he killed more than ten thousand people.

sentences.zh: 尚書令陽球常拊髀發憤曰：「若陽球作司隸，此曹子安得容乎！

translations.literal: Master of Writing Yang Qiu would often slap his thigh in rage and say: "If Yang Qiu were Metropolitan Commandant, how could these fellows find a place!
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Yang Qiu often slapped his thigh in fury and said, "If I were Metropolitan Commandant, how could these men survive!

sentences.zh: 」即而球果遷司隸。

translations.literal: Before long Qiu was indeed transferred to Metropolitan Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yang Qiu was indeed made Metropolitan Commandant.

sentences.zh: 甫使門生於京兆界辜榷官財物七千餘萬，京兆尹楊彪發其奸，言之司隸。

translations.literal: Fu had a student retainers monopolize and levy official goods in the capital region to the value of more than seventy million; the Intendant of the Capital Yang Biao exposed the crime and reported it to the Metropolitan Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's retainers extorted more than seventy million in official goods in the capital region; Capital Intendant Yang Biao exposed the crime and reported it to the Metropolitan Commandant.

sentences.zh: 彪，賜之子也。

translations.literal: Biao was the son of Yang Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Biao was the son of Yang Ci.

sentences.zh: 時甫休沐裡捨，熲方以日食自劾。

translations.literal: At the time Fu was on leave at his village residence, and Yong had just impeached himself over the solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu was then on leave at his estate, and Duan Yong had just submitted a self-impeachment over the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 球詣闕謝恩，因奏甫、熲及中常侍淳於登、袁赦、封□羽等罪惡，辛巳，悉收甫、熲等送洛陽獄，及甫子永樂少府萌、沛相吉。

translations.literal: Qiu went to the palace to give thanks for his appointment and thereupon memorialized the crimes of Fu, Yong, and the Regular Palace Attendants Chunyu Deng, Yuan She, Feng Xu, and others; on the day xinsi all were seized—Fu, Yong, and the rest—and sent to Luoyang prison, together with Fu's son Meng, Superintendent of the Yongle Palace, and Ji, Administrator of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu went to court to thank the emperor for his appointment and memorialized the crimes of Fu, Yong, and the eunuchs Chunyu Deng, Yuan She, Feng Xu, and others. On xinsi all were arrested—Fu, Yong, and the rest—and sent to Luoyang prison, along with Fu's son Meng, Superintendent of the Yongle Palace, and Ji, Administrator of Pei.

sentences.zh: 球自臨考甫等，五毒備極；

translations.literal: Qiu personally presided over the interrogation of Fu and the others, employing the five tortures to the utmost;
translations.idiomatic: Qiu personally interrogated Fu and the others, applying every form of torture;

sentences.zh: 萌先嘗為司隸，乃謂球曰：「父子既當伏誅，亦以先後之義，少以楚毒假借老父。

translations.literal: Meng had formerly served as Metropolitan Commandant and said to Qiu: "Father and son must both submit to execution; still, by the principle of precedence, spare the old father a little of the Chu torture.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, who had once been Metropolitan Commandant himself, said to Qiu, "Father and son must both die—but by the rule of precedence, spare my aged father some of the beating.

sentences.zh: 」球曰：「爾罪惡無狀，死不滅責，乃欲論先後求假借邪！

translations.literal: Qiu said: "Your crimes are beyond description; death cannot extinguish your guilt—yet you wish to plead precedence and beg for leniency!
translations.idiomatic: Qiu said, "Your crimes are beyond measure—death cannot expiate them—and you plead precedence for leniency!

sentences.zh: 」萌乃罵曰：「爾前奉事吾父子如奴，奴敢反汝主乎！

translations.literal: Meng then cursed: "You once served my father and son like a slave—does a slave dare turn against his master!
translations.idiomatic: Meng cursed, "You once served us father and son like a slave—does a slave dare turn on his master!

sentences.zh: 今日臨坑相擠，行自及也！

translations.literal: Today at the pit's edge we push each other—you will soon reach it yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Today at the pit's edge we shove each other—you will soon fall in yourself!

sentences.zh: 」球使以土窒萌口，箠撲交至，父子悉死於杖下；

translations.literal: Qiu had earth stuffed into Meng's mouth; blows from cudgels rained down, and father and son both died under the staves;
translations.idiomatic: Qiu had earth stuffed into Meng's mouth; cudgels rained down until father and son both died under the blows;

sentences.zh: 熲亦自殺。

translations.literal: Yong also killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yong also took his own life.

sentences.zh: 乃僵磔甫屍於夏城門，大署榜曰：「賊臣王甫。

translations.literal: Fu's corpse was then exposed and dismembered at the Xia Gate, with a large placard inscribed: "The traitor minister Wang Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's corpse was dismembered and displayed at the Xia Gate, with a placard reading, "Traitor minister Wang Fu.

sentences.zh: 」盡沒入其財產，妻子皆徙比景。

translations.literal: All his property was confiscated, and his wife and children were all banished to Bijing.
translations.idiomatic: All his property was confiscated, and his wife and children were exiled to Bijing.

sentences.zh: 球既誅甫，欲以次表曹節等，乃敕中都官從事曰：「且先去權貴大猾，乃議其餘耳。

translations.literal: After Qiu had executed Fu, he wished to memorialize Cao Jie and the rest in turn, and therefore instructed the Director of Retainers for the Inner Palace: "First remove the powerful magnates and great villains; then discuss the rest.
translations.idiomatic: After executing Fu, Qiu meant to indict Cao Jie and the rest in turn. He instructed the Director of Retainers, "First take the powerful ringleaders; then deal with the rest.

sentences.zh: 公卿豪右若袁氏兒輩，從事自辦之，何須校尉邪！

translations.literal: For grandees and powerful families like the Yuan clan youngsters, the Director may handle them himself—what need of the Commandant!
translations.idiomatic: For grandees like the Yuan clan, you may handle them yourself—what need of the Commandant!

sentences.zh: 」權門聞之，莫不屏氣。

translations.literal: When the powerful families heard this, none failed to hold their breath.
translations.idiomatic: When the powerful families heard this, they all held their breath.

sentences.zh: 曹節等皆不敢出沐。

translations.literal: Cao Jie and the rest did not dare go out on leave to bathe.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie and the rest did not dare leave their posts even for ritual bathing.

sentences.zh: 會順帝虞貴人葬，百官會喪還，曹節見磔甫屍道次，慨然抆淚曰：「我曹可自相食，何宜使犬舐其汁乎！

translations.literal: It happened that at the burial of the Honored Lady Yu of Emperor Shun the hundred officials were returning from the funeral assembly when Cao Jie saw Fu's dismembered corpse by the roadside; sighing, he wiped away tears and said: "We fellows may devour one another—how is it fitting to let dogs lick his juices!
translations.idiomatic: When the officials returned from the funeral of Emperor Shun's Honored Lady Yu, Cao Jie saw Fu's dismembered corpse by the road. He sighed and wiped away tears: "We may devour one another—but why let dogs lick his blood!

sentences.zh: 」語諸常侍：「今且俱入，勿過裡捨也。

translations.literal: He told the Regular Attendants: "Today let us all enter together; do not pass by our village residences.
translations.idiomatic: He told the eunuchs, "Today we all enter the palace together—do not stop at our estates.

sentences.zh: 」節直入省，白帝曰：「陽球故酷暴吏，前三府奏當免官，以九江微功，復見擢用。

translations.literal: Jie went straight into the Secretariat and reported to the Emperor: "Yang Qiu is by origin a cruel and violent official; the Three Excellencies thrice memorialized that he should be dismissed from office, yet for slight merit at Jiujiang he was again promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Jie went straight to the Secretariat and told the emperor, "Yang Qiu is a brutal official by nature; the Three Excellencies thrice recommended his dismissal, yet for minor service at Jiujiang he was promoted again.

sentences.zh: 愆過之人，好為妄作，不宜使在司隸，以騁毒虐。

translations.literal: A man of faults delights in reckless acts; he should not be kept as Metropolitan Commandant to unleash his cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: A man of faults loves reckless action; he must not hold the Metropolitan Commandancy and unleash his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃徙球為衛尉。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon transferred Qiu to Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then transferred Qiu to Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 時球出謁陵，節敕尚書令召拜，不得稽留尺一。

translations.literal: At the time Qiu was out paying respects at the tombs; Jie ordered the Master of Writing to summon and invest him, allowing no delay of the inch-wide edict.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was then away at the imperial tombs; Jie ordered the Master of Writing to summon him at once, allowing no delay.

sentences.zh: 球被召急，因求見帝，叩頭曰：「臣無清高之行，橫蒙鷹犬之任，前雖誅王甫、段熲，蓋狐狸小丑，未足宣示天下。

translations.literal: Qiu, urgently summoned, sought an audience with the Emperor and kowtowed, saying: "Your servant has no conduct of lofty purity, yet was rashly entrusted with the role of hawk and hound; though I earlier executed Wang Fu and Duan Yong, they were but foxes and petty clowns, insufficient to proclaim to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned in haste, Qiu sought audience and kowtowed: "I have no lofty virtue, yet was made the emperor's hawk and hound. Though I executed Wang Fu and Duan Yong, they were mere foxes and petty villains—not enough to show the realm.

sentences.zh: 願假臣一月，必令豺狼鴟梟各服其辜。

translations.literal: I beg to be granted one month; I will surely make wolves, owls, and vultures each answer for their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Grant me one month, and I will make every wolf and owl answer for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 」叩頭流血。

translations.literal: He kowtowed until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed until his forehead bled.

sentences.zh: 殿上呵叱曰：「衛尉扞詔邪！

translations.literal: From the hall came a shout of rebuke: "Commandant of the Guards, do you resist the edict!
translations.idiomatic: From the hall came a shout: "Commandant of the Guards, do you defy the edict!

sentences.zh: 」至於再三，乃受拜。

translations.literal: Only after three and four times did he accept the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Only after repeated rebukes did he accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 於是曹節、朱瑀等權勢復盛。

translations.literal: Thereupon the power of Cao Jie, Zhu Yu, and the rest flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Cao Jie, Zhu Yu, and their faction regained their power.

sentences.zh: 節領尚書令。

translations.literal: Jie held the post of Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Jie held the post of Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 郎中梁人審忠上書曰：「陛下即位之初，未能萬機，皇太后念在撫育，權時攝政，故中常侍蘇康、管霸應時誅殄。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Palace Shen Zhong of Liang submitted a memorial saying: "When Your Majesty first ascended the throne you could not yet handle the myriad affairs; the Empress Dowager, mindful of nurturing, temporarily held regency—therefore the Regular Palace Attendants Su Kang and Guan Ba were timely executed and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Palace Shen Zhong of Liang memorialized, "When Your Majesty first ascended the throne you could not yet govern; the Empress Dowager ruled temporarily, and the eunuchs Su Kang and Guan Ba were rightly executed.

sentences.zh: 太傅陳蕃、大將軍竇武考其黨與，志清朝政。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Chen Fan and General-in-Chief Dou Wu investigated their partisans, intending to purify the court government.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Chen Fan and General-in-Chief Dou Wu investigated their faction, intending to purify the court.

sentences.zh: 華容侯朱瑀知事覺露，禍及其身，遂興造逆謀，作亂王室，撞蹋省闥，執奪璽綬，迫脅陛下，聚會群臣，離間骨肉母子之恩，遂誅蕃、武及尹勳等。

translations.literal: Marquis of Huarong Zhu Yu, knowing the affair was exposed and disaster would reach his person, thereupon raised a treasonous plot, made rebellion in the royal house, battered and trampled the gates of the Secretariat, seized the seal and cord, coerced Your Majesty, assembled the ministers, sundered the affection between flesh and bone, mother and son, and thus executed Fan, Wu, Yin Xun, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Huarong Zhu Yu, seeing exposure and ruin before him, raised a treasonous plot, stormed the Secretariat, seized the imperial seal, coerced Your Majesty, assembled ministers, sundered mother and son, and executed Fan, Wu, Yin Xun, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 因共割裂城社，自相封賞，父子兄弟，被蒙尊榮，素所親厚，布在州郡，或登九列，或據三司。

translations.literal: They together carved up altars of earth and walled cities, rewarding one another with enfeoffments; fathers, sons, and brothers were clothed in honor and glory; those they had long favored were spread through the provinces and commanderies, some ascending to the nine ranks, some holding the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: They carved up the realm among themselves, enfeoffing one another; fathers, sons, and brothers were showered with honors; their favorites filled the provinces, some reaching the highest ranks, some holding the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 不惟祿重位尊之責，而苟營私門，多蓄財貨，繕修第捨，連裡竟巷，盜取御水，以作漁釣，車馬服玩，擬於天家。

translations.literal: They did not merely bear the responsibility of heavy salary and exalted rank, but recklessly schemed for private gain, amassed much wealth, repaired mansions stretching lane to lane, stole imperial water for fishing, and made carriages, horses, garments, and curios rivaling the Son of Heaven's household.
translations.idiomatic: They did not merely enjoy fat salaries and high rank but schemed for private gain, hoarded wealth, built mansions block after block, diverted imperial water for fishing, and equipped themselves with carriages, horses, and luxuries rivaling the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 群公卿士，杜口吞聲，莫敢有言；

translations.literal: the host of dukes, ministers, and gentlemen sealed their mouths and swallowed their voices, none daring to speak;
translations.idiomatic: The host of ministers sealed their lips and dared not speak;

sentences.zh: 州牧郡守，承順風旨，辟召選舉，釋賢取愚。

translations.literal: regional governors and commandery administrators followed the prevailing wind, in summons and selection releasing the worthy and taking the foolish.
translations.idiomatic: governors and prefects followed their lead in appointments, rejecting the worthy and choosing fools.

sentences.zh: 故蟲蝗為之生，夷寇為之起，天意憤盈，積十餘年，故頻歲日食於上，地震於下，所以譴戒人主，欲令覺悟，誅金甘無狀。

translations.literal: Therefore locusts and insects were born for them, barbarian raiders rose for them; Heaven's intent was full of wrath, accumulating for more than ten years—hence year after year solar eclipses above and earthquakes below, thereby reproving and warning the ruler, wishing to make him awaken and execute the shameless men of metal and sweet.
translations.idiomatic: Hence locusts and barbarian raids; Heaven's wrath has built for more than ten years—hence repeated eclipses above and earthquakes below, warning the sovereign to awaken and destroy these shameless villains.

sentences.zh: 昔高宗以雉雊之變，故獲中興之功；

translations.literal: In the past Gaozong, because of the transformation of a pheasant's crow, therefore obtained the achievement of restoration;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong once turned a pheasant's crow into restoration of the dynasty;

sentences.zh: 近者神祇啟悟陛下，發赫斯之怒，故王甫父子應時馘截，路人士女莫不稱善，若除父母之仇。

translations.literal: Recently the spirits enlightened Your Majesty and roused a majestic wrath, and therefore Wang Fu father and son were timely beheaded; travelers, gentlemen, and women on the road all praised it as if avenging parents.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the spirits awakened Your Majesty to majestic wrath, and Wang Fu and his son were executed; travelers and townsfolk praised it as though avenging their own parents.

sentences.zh: 誠恐陛下復忍孽臣之類，不悉殄滅。

translations.literal: I truly fear Your Majesty will again spare the class of wicked ministers and not utterly exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: I truly fear Your Majesty will again spare such wicked ministers and not destroy them utterly.

sentences.zh: 昔秦信趙高，以危其國；

translations.literal: In the past Qin trusted Zhao Gao and thereby endangered its state;
translations.idiomatic: Qin once trusted Zhao Gao and endangered the realm;

sentences.zh: 吳使刑人，身遘其禍。

translations.literal: Wu employed a man of punishment and personally encountered the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Wu employed a criminal as minister and suffered the consequence himself.

sentences.zh: 今以不忍之恩，赦夷族之罪，奸謀一成，悔亦何及！

translations.literal: Now by an indulgent kindness you pardon crimes deserving extermination of the clan—once treacherous plots are formed, what use is regret!
translations.idiomatic: Now, by misplaced mercy, you pardon crimes deserving clan extermination—once treason takes shape, regret will be too late!

sentences.zh: 臣為郎十五年，皆耳目聞見，瑀之所為，誠皇天所不復赦。

translations.literal: Your servant has been a Gentleman for fifteen years, all heard and seen with my own ears and eyes; what Yu has done is truly what August Heaven will not pardon again.
translations.idiomatic: I have served as a Gentleman for fifteen years and witnessed it all; what Zhu Yu has done Heaven itself will not forgive.

sentences.zh: 願陛下留漏刻之聽，裁省臣表，掃滅丑類，以答天怒。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to reserve the hearing of the clepsydra's drops, examine and reduce my memorial, sweep away the vile sort, and answer Heaven's wrath.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to heed this memorial, destroy these vile men, and answer Heaven's wrath.

sentences.zh: 與瑀考驗，有不如言，願受湯鑊之誅，妻子並徙，以絕妄言之路。

translations.literal: If investigated against Yu my words prove false, I am willing to suffer execution in boiling cauldron, my wife and children banished together, to cut off the path of reckless speech.
translations.idiomatic: If investigation proves me wrong about Zhu Yu, I accept death in the boiling cauldron and exile for my wife and children—to cut off all false speech.

sentences.zh: 」章寢不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was shelved without response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was shelved without response.

sentences.zh: 中常侍呂強清忠奉公，帝以眾例封為都鄉侯，強固辭不受，因上疏陳事曰：「臣聞高祖重約，非功臣不侯，所以重天爵、明勸戒也。

translations.literal: The Regular Palace Attendant Lü Qiang was pure, loyal, and devoted to the public; the Emperor by the common precedent enfeoffed him as Marquis of the Capital District, but Qiang firmly declined and would not accept, and therefore submitted a memorial stating affairs: "Your servant has heard that Gaozu valued covenants—none but meritorious ministers were enfeoffed as marquises; thus he honored Heaven's nobility and made encouragement and warning clear.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Palace Attendant Lü Qiang was pure and loyal; the emperor offered to enfeoff him as Marquis of the Capital District by precedent, but Qiang firmly declined and memorialized, "I have heard that Emperor Gaozu honored covenants—only meritorious ministers were enfeoffed—thereby honoring Heaven's rank and making reward and warning clear.

sentences.zh: 中常侍曹節等，宦官祐薄，品卑人賤，讒諂媚主，佞邪徼寵，有趙高之禍，未被轘裂之誅。

translations.literal: The Regular Palace Attendants Cao Jie and the rest are eunuchs of thin blessing, low in rank and base in person, slandering and flattering the lord, crafty and wicked in scheming for favor—they bear Zhao Gao's calamity yet have not suffered the punishment of being torn apart by chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie and the other eunuchs are men of low birth who flatter and slander, scheme for favor, and bring Zhao Gao's calamity—yet have not suffered torn-apart execution.

sentences.zh: 陛下不悟，妄授茅土，開國承家，小人是用，又並及家人，重金兼紫，交結邪黨，下比群佞。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not awaken but rashly bestows feudal soil, establishing states and continuing families—petty men are employed, and their households are included as well, heavy gold combined with purple, forming factions with wicked cliques, comparing themselves below to the host of flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not see it but rashly grants fiefs, ennobling petty men and their whole households with gold and purple rank, forming wicked factions and allying with flatterers.

sentences.zh: 陰陽乖剌，稼穡荒蕪，人用不康，罔不由茲。

translations.literal: Yin and yang are perverse and cutting; crops lie waste and overgrown; the people's use is not at peace—none of this is not from this cause.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang are out of harmony, fields lie waste, and the people suffer unrest—all from this cause.

sentences.zh: 臣誠知封事已行，言之無逮，所以冒死干觸陳愚忠者，實願陛下損改既謬，從此一止。

translations.literal: Your servant truly knows the enfeoffments are already done and speech cannot reach them; the reason I risk death in offense to state foolish loyalty is truly to wish Your Majesty to reduce and change what is already wrong, and from this point stop.
translations.idiomatic: I know the enfeoffments are already done and words come too late; I risk death to speak because I truly wish Your Majesty to correct this error and stop here.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞後宮采女數千餘人，衣食之費日數百金，比谷雖賤而戶有饑色，案法當貴而今更賤者，由賦發繁數，以解縣官，寒不敢衣，饑不敢食，民有斯厄而莫之恤。

translations.literal: Your servant further hears that in the inner palace there are several thousand palace women; the cost of food and clothing is several hundred in gold each day. Though grain is cheap by comparison, households show the color of hunger; by law grain ought to be costly yet now is cheaper—because levies are issued frequently to relieve the county offices; in cold they dare not clothe themselves, in hunger they dare not eat; the people have this distress yet none pities them.
translations.idiomatic: I further hear that the inner palace holds several thousand women, costing hundreds in gold daily for food and clothing. Though grain is cheap, households show hunger; grain should be dear by law yet is cheap because taxes are levied repeatedly to fill official coffers—the people dare not clothe themselves against cold or eat against hunger, yet none pity their distress.

sentences.zh: 宮女無用，填積後庭，天下雖復盡力耕桑，猶不能供。

translations.literal: Palace women are useless, piled up in the rear court; though all under Heaven again exert utmost strength in farming and sericulture, still they cannot supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Useless palace women fill the rear court; though the realm farms and mulberries with all its strength, it still cannot supply them.

sentences.zh: 又，前召議郎蔡邕對問於金商門，邕不敢懷道迷國，而切言極對，毀刺貴臣，譏呵宦官。

translations.literal: Moreover, earlier Consulting Gentleman Cai Yong was summoned for questioning at the Jingshang Gate; Yong did not dare harbor the Way and mislead the state, but spoke bluntly to the utmost, denouncing great ministers and mocking the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Consulting Gentleman Cai Yong was earlier summoned to answer questions at the Jingshang Gate. He did not hide the truth to mislead the state but spoke bluntly, denouncing great ministers and rebuking the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 陛下不密其言，至令宣露，群邪項領，膏脣拭舌，競欲咀嚼，造作飛條。

translations.literal: Your Majesty did not keep his words secret, until they were proclaimed and exposed; the host of wicked men stretched their necks, greased their lips and wiped their tongues, competing to chew him up and fabricating flying indictments.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty did not keep his words secret, and they were leaked. The wicked stretched their necks, licked their lips, and competed to destroy him, fabricating secret indictments.

sentences.zh: 陛下回受誹謗，致邕刑罪，室家徙放，老幼流離，豈不負忠臣哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty in turn accepted slander, bringing upon Yong criminal punishment; his household was banished, old and young cast adrift—have you not failed a loyal minister!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty accepted slander instead, punished Yong, and exiled his household until old and young were scattered—have you not betrayed a loyal minister!

sentences.zh: 今群臣皆以邕為戒，上畏不測之難，下懼劍客之害，臣知朝廷不復得聞忠言矣！

translations.literal: Now the host of ministers all take Yong as a warning; above they fear unforeseen calamity, below they dread harm from swordsmen—I know the court will no longer hear loyal words!
translations.idiomatic: Now every minister takes Yong as a warning—fearing disaster above and assassins below. I know the court will never again hear frank counsel!

sentences.zh: 故太尉段熲，武勇冠世，習於邊事，垂發服戎，功成皓首，歷事二主，勳烈獨昭。

translations.literal: Former Grand Commandant Duan Yong's martial valor crowned the age; he was practiced in frontier affairs, took up arms with hair hanging down, achieved merit with head turned white, served two rulers, his achievements and glory uniquely brilliant.
translations.idiomatic: Former Grand Commandant Duan Yong's martial valor was unmatched. Skilled in frontier warfare, he took up arms in youth and won glory in old age, serving two emperors with brilliant merit.

sentences.zh: 陛下既已式序，位登台司，而為司隸校尉陽球所見誣脅，一身既斃，而妻子遠播，天下惆悵，功臣失望。

translations.literal: Your Majesty had already by ritual ranked him and placed him in the highest office, yet he was seen and coerced by false charges from Metropolitan Commandant Yang Qiu; his person was already dead and his wife and children cast far abroad—all under Heaven were sorrowful, meritorious servants disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty had honored him with the highest office, yet Metropolitan Commandant Yang Qiu framed him. He was killed, his family exiled, the realm grieved, and worthy servants lost hope.

sentences.zh: 宜征邕更加授任，反熲家屬，則忠貞路開，眾怨以弭矣。

translations.literal: You ought to summon Yong and further grant him office, restore Yong's household—then the path of loyalty and integrity will open and the multitude's resentment be quelled.
translations.idiomatic: Summon Yong and restore him to office; recall Duan Yong's family—then the path of loyalty will reopen and public resentment be stilled.

sentences.zh: 」帝知其忠而不能用。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew his loyalty yet could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew he was loyal but could not act on it.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the empire was granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 上祿長和海上言：「禮，從祖兄弟別居異財，恩義已輕，服屬疏末。

translations.literal: He Shang of Shangluo county memorialized: "By ritual, cousins of the same great-grandfather who live apart with separate property already have light affection and obligation; the degree of mourning attire is remote and last.
translations.idiomatic: He Shang of Shangluo county memorialized, "By ritual, cousins who live apart with separate property owe only light obligations; mourning ties are remote.

sentences.zh: 而今黨人錮及五族，既乖典訓之文，有謬經常之法。

translations.literal: Yet now the proscription of partisans extends to five clans—this already departs from the text of canonical instruction and errs against constant law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the partisan proscription now reaches five clans—contrary to canonical teaching and regular law.

sentences.zh: 」帝覽之而悟，於是黨錮自從祖以下皆得解釋。

translations.literal: The Emperor read it and was enlightened; thereupon the partisan proscription from second cousins downward was all released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and understood; the partisan ban was lifted for all kin from second cousins downward.

sentences.zh: 五月，以衛尉劉寬為太尉。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Commandant of the Guards Liu Kuan was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Commandant of the Guards Liu Kuan was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 護匈奴中郎將張修與南單于呼征不相能，修擅斬之，更立右賢王羌渠為單于。

translations.literal: Protector-General of the Xiongnu Zhang Xiu and the Southern Chanyu Huzheng were incompatible; Xiu on his own authority executed him and installed the Right Worthy King Qiangqu as Chanyu in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Protector-General of the Xiongnu Zhang Xiu quarreled with Southern Chanyu Huzheng, executed him on his own authority, and installed Right Worthy King Qiangqu as Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，修坐不先請而擅誅殺，檻車征詣廷尉，死。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Xiu was convicted of not requesting permission beforehand but killing on his own authority; he was summoned in a prisoner cart to the Court Commandant and died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Xiu was convicted of executing without prior authorization, summoned in a prisoner cart to the Court Commandant, and put to death.

sentences.zh: 初，司徒劉郃兄侍中鯈與竇武同謀，俱死。

translations.literal: Earlier, the elder brother of Minister over the Masses Liu He, Palace Attendant Tiao, had joined in Dou Wu's plot and both died.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu He's elder brother, Palace Attendant Tiao, had joined Dou Wu's plot and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 永樂少府陳球說郃曰：「公出自宗室，位登台鼎，天下瞻望，社稷鎮衛，豈得雷同，容容無違而已。

translations.literal: Superintendent of the Yongle Palace Chen Qiu said to He: "You spring from the imperial clan, your rank mounts to the tripod cauldron; all under Heaven look to you, the altars of state are guarded by you—how can you merely echo others and be easygoing without opposition!
translations.idiomatic: Superintendent of the Yongle Palace Chen Qiu urged He, "You are of the imperial clan and hold the highest office; the realm looks to you to guard the altars of state—how can you merely echo others and never resist!

sentences.zh: 今曹節等放縱為害，而久在左右，又公兄侍中受害節等，今可表徙衛尉陽球為司隸校尉，以次收節等誅之，政出聖主，天下太平，可翹足而待也！

translations.literal: Now Cao Jie and the rest run riot in harm yet long remain at your side; moreover your brother the Palace Attendant was victimized by Jie and the rest. Now you may memorialize to transfer Commandant of the Guards Yang Qiu to Metropolitan Commandant and in turn seize Jie and the rest and execute them—government will issue from the sage lord, all under Heaven will be at peace, and you may wait with feet crossed!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie and his faction run rampant at the emperor's side, and they killed your brother the Palace Attendant. Memorialize to make Yang Qiu Metropolitan Commandant and arrest Jie and the rest in turn. Government will return to the sage ruler, peace will come, and you need only wait!

sentences.zh: 」郃曰：「凶豎多耳目，恐事未會，先受其禍。

translations.literal: He said: "The vicious fellows have many eyes and ears; I fear before the affair is joined I will first suffer calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Those villains have spies everywhere—I fear the plot will fail and I will suffer first.

sentences.zh: 」尚書劉納曰：「為國棟樑，傾危不持，焉用延彼相邪！

translations.literal: Master of Writing Liu Na said: "As a pillar of the state, if you do not support it in tilting peril, of what use is it to prolong that minister!
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Liu Na said, "As a pillar of the state, if you will not support it in crisis, what use is such a minister!

sentences.zh: 」郃許諾，亦與陽球結謀。

translations.literal: He promised, and also formed a plot with Yang Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed and also plotted with Yang Qiu.

sentences.zh: 球小妻，程璜之女，由是節等頗得聞知，乃重賂璜，且脅之。

translations.literal: Qiu's junior wife was the daughter of Cheng Huang; thereby Jie and the rest came to hear quite a bit, and therefore heavily bribed Huang and also coerced him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's junior wife was Cheng Huang's daughter, so Jie and the rest learned of the plot. They bribed Huang heavily and threatened him.

sentences.zh: 璜懼迫，以球謀告節，節因共白帝曰：「郃與劉納、陳球、陽球交通書疏，謀議不軌。

translations.literal: Huang, in fear and under pressure, reported Qiu's plot to Jie; Jie thereupon together reported to the Emperor: "He, Liu Na, Chen Qiu, and Yang Qiu exchange letters and documents, plotting unorthodox designs.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, frightened, revealed the plot to Jie. Jie reported to the emperor, "He, Liu Na, Chen Qiu, and Yang Qiu exchange letters and plot treason.

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲申，劉郃、陳球、劉納、陽球皆下獄死。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiashen, Liu He, Chen Qiu, Liu Na, and Yang Qiu were all cast into prison and died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on jiashen, Liu He, Chen Qiu, Liu Na, and Yang Qiu were all thrown into prison and put to death.

sentences.zh: 巴郡板楯蠻反，遣御史中丞蕭瑗督益州刺史討之，不克。

translations.literal: The Banshun barbarians of Ba commandery rebelled; Imperial Secretary Xiao Yuan was sent to supervise the Regional Inspector of Yizhou in punishing them, but he could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The Banshun tribes of Ba commandery rebelled. Imperial Secretary Xiao Yuan supervised the Regional Inspector of Yizhou in suppressing them but failed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以光祿勳楊賜為司徒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yang Ci was appointed Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yang Ci was made Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑寇幽、并二州。

translations.literal: The Xianbei raided the two provinces of You and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei raided You and Bing provinces.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸酉，赦天下。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day guiyou, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on guiyou, the empire was granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，江夏蠻反。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Jiangxia barbarians rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, the Jiangxia tribes rebelled.

sentences.zh: 秋，酒泉地震。

translations.literal: In autumn, Jiuquan was shaken by an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn an earthquake struck Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 冬，有星孛於狼、弧。

translations.literal: In winter, a broom star appeared in the Wolf and Arc.
translations.idiomatic: In winter a comet appeared in the Wolf and Arc constellations.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑寇幽、并二州。

translations.literal: The Xianbei raided the two provinces of You and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei again raided You and Bing provinces.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己巳，立貴人何氏為皇后。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day jisi, the Honored Lady of the He clan was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jisi, Honored Lady He was made empress.

sentences.zh: 征後兄穎川太守進為侍中。

translations.literal: The empress's elder brother Jin, Grand Administrator of Yingchuan, was summoned and made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's elder brother He Jin, Grand Administrator of Yingchuan, was summoned and made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後本南陽屠家，以選入掖庭，生皇子辯，故立之。

translations.literal: The empress was originally of a butcher's family in Nanyang; by selection she entered the Rear Palace, bore the prince Bian, and therefore was established.
translations.idiomatic: The empress came from a butcher's family in Nanyang, entered the palace by selection, bore Prince Bian, and was therefore enthroned.

sentences.zh: 是歲作罼圭、靈昆苑。

translations.literal: That year the Bigui and Lingkun parks were constructed.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Bigui and Lingkun parks were built.

sentences.zh: 司徒楊賜諫曰：「先帝之制，左開鴻池，右作上林，不奢不約，以合禮中。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Yang Ci remonstrated: "The former emperor's regulation opened Hongchi on the left and made Shanglin on the right—not extravagant, not austere, to accord with the mean of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Yang Ci remonstrated, "The former emperor's rule opened Hongchi on the left and Shanglin on the right—neither extravagant nor austere, fitting the mean of ritual.

sentences.zh: 今猥規郊城之地以為苑囿，壞沃衍，廢田園，驅居民，畜禽獸，殆非所謂若保赤子之義。

translations.literal: Now you rashly plan suburban city lands as park and preserve, ruining fertile expanses, abandoning fields and gardens, driving out residents, raising birds and beasts—this is hardly what is called the principle of cherishing an infant.
translations.idiomatic: Now you plan to turn suburban lands into parks, ruining fertile fields, abandoning farms, driving out residents, and raising game—hardly the way to cherish the people like infants.

sentences.zh: 今城外之苑已有五六，可以逞情意，順四節也。

translations.literal: Now outside the city there are already five or six parks, enough to indulge intent and follow the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: There are already five or six parks outside the city—enough to satisfy pleasure and follow the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 宜惟夏禹卑宮、太宗露台之意，以尉下民之勞。

translations.literal: You ought to consider the intent of Xia Yu's humble palace and Taizong's terrace of earth, to comfort the toil of the people below.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Yu the Great's humble palace and Taizong's earthen terrace, and ease the people's labor.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，帝欲止，以問侍中任芝、樂松；

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor wished to stop and questioned Palace Attendants Ren Zhi and Yue Song;
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor wished to stop and asked Palace Attendants Ren Zhi and Yue Song;

sentences.zh: 對曰：「昔文王之囿百里，人以為小；

translations.literal: they replied: "In the past King Wen's park was a hundred li, yet people thought it small;
translations.idiomatic: they answered, "King Wen's park was a hundred li, yet people thought it small;

sentences.zh: 齊宣五里，人以為大。

translations.literal: King Xuan of Qi's was five li, yet people thought it large.
translations.idiomatic: King Xuan of Qi's was five li, yet people thought it large.

sentences.zh: 今與百姓共之，無害於政也。

translations.literal: Now sharing it with the common people does no harm to government.
translations.idiomatic: Sharing it with the people does no harm to government.

sentences.zh: 」帝悅，遂為之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and thereupon proceeded with it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and proceeded with it.

sentences.zh: 巴郡板楯蠻反。

translations.literal: The Banshun barbarians of Ba commandery rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Banshun tribes of Ba commandery rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧、桂陽賊攻郡縣，零陵太守楊璇制馬車數十乘，以排囊盛石灰於車上，系布索於馬尾；

translations.literal: Bandits in Cangwu and Guiyang attacked commanderies and counties; the Grand Administrator of Lingling Yang Xuan devised several dozen horse-drawn carts, with bellows-bags holding lime on the carts, and cloth ropes tied to the horses' tails;
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in Cangwu and Guiyang attacked commanderies and counties. Grand Administrator of Lingling Yang Xuan built several dozen horse-drawn carts fitted with bellows bags of lime and cloth ropes tied to the horses' tails;

sentences.zh: 又為兵車，專彀弓弩。

translations.literal: he also made war carts devoted solely to drawing crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: and war carts armed only with crossbows.

sentences.zh: 及戰，令馬車居前，順風鼓灰，賊不得視，因以火燒布然，馬驚，奔突賊陣，因使後車弓弩亂髮，鉦鼓鳴震，群盜波駭破散，追逐傷斬無數，梟其渠帥，郡境以清。

translations.literal: When battle came, he ordered the horse carts forward; with the wind they blew lime, and the bandits could not see; then they set fire to the cloth, which blazed, the horses panicked and charged the bandit formation; thereupon the rear carts shot crossbows in disorder, gongs and drums thundered, the host of robbers were shattered like waves in terror and scattered; pursuit wounded and beheaded countless, the ringleaders were displayed, and the commandery borders were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he sent the lime carts forward; with the wind they blew dust into the enemy's eyes. They set the cloth alight, panicking the horses into the bandit ranks, while crossbow carts behind rained bolts amid gongs and drums. The bandits broke in terror; pursuit killed countless and captured the leaders, and the commandery was pacified.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史趙凱誣奏璇實非身破賊，而妄有其功；

translations.literal: Regional Inspector of Jingzhou Zhao Kai falsely memorialized that Xuan had not personally broken the bandits but falsely claimed the merit;
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector of Jingzhou Zhao Kai falsely reported that Xuan had not personally defeated the bandits but falsely claimed credit;

sentences.zh: 璇與相章奏。

translations.literal: Xuan in turn memorialized in rebuttal.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan memorialized in rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 凱有黨助，遂檻車征璇，防禁嚴密，無由自訟；

translations.literal: Kai had partisan helpers, and therefore Xuan was summoned in a prisoner cart with strict confinement, with no means to plead his own case;
translations.idiomatic: Kai had partisan allies, and Xuan was summoned in a prisoner cart under strict guard, unable to plead his case;

sentences.zh: 乃噬臂出血，書衣為章，具陳破賊形勢，及言凱所誣狀，潛令親屬詣厥通之。

translations.literal: he thereupon bit his arm until blood flowed, wrote on his garment as a memorial, fully stating the situation of defeating the bandits and declaring the false charges of Kai, and secretly ordered kin to go to the capital and have it delivered.
translations.idiomatic: he bit his arm until it bled, wrote his defense on his garment, described how he had defeated the bandits and exposed Kai's false charges, and secretly sent kin to deliver it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔書原璇，拜議郎；

translations.literal: An imperial edict pardoned Xuan and appointed him Consulting Gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned Xuan and appointed him Consulting Gentleman;

sentences.zh: 凱受誣人之罪。

translations.literal: Kai received the crime of falsely accusing others.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was punished for false accusation.

sentences.zh: 璇，喬之弟也。

translations.literal: Xuan was the younger brother of Yang Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was the younger brother of Yang Qiao.
